title: SCM Strategy & Operations Manager (D2C MX)
jd_text: Position Summary This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship. Headquartered in Plano, TX, Samsung Electronics America (SEA) is a leader in mobile technologies, consumer electronics, home appliances, enterprise solutions and networks systems. Across each of these areas, our work drives innovation, economic growth and workforce opportunity in the United States. For nearly five decades, Samsung has been at the forefront of technological advancements, investing over $100 billion and creating more than 20,000 jobs nationwide. Our mission? To integrate cutting-edge products, services, and AI technology to deliver smarter, sustainable, and more connected experiences that empower people to live better. As a wholly owned subsidiary of Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd., SEA offers opportunities to work alongside global visionary thinkers and innovators who are passionate about making a difference. Explore the exciting opportunities at Samsung Electronics America and discover how you can make an impact. To learn more, visit Samsung.com. For the latest news, visit news.samsung.com/us. Role and Responsibilities Role Overview The SCM Strategy and Operations Manager will support Samsung Direct to Consumer (D2C) channel for Mobile Experience (MX) and will be responsible for 3 major areas: 1. Lead and Manage Next SCM and back-office integration, enhancements and Master Data Management for D2C 2. Work with all central teams to ensure D2C planned supply is timely secured and made available for sales (Stock transfer process and interface with central SCM, AP2, logistics and fulfillment teams) 3. Support Demand Planning analysis and provide insights to manage multi-channel inventory (s.com, BOPIS). The individual also is expected to drive both tactical execution and long-term strategic improvements, while championing the adoption of AI technologies and process automation to elevate supply chain efficiency and effectiveness across the organization. Key Responsibilities · Lead SCM Systems and back office for D2C MX business · Manage D2C Master Data Management with strong understanding of supply chain systems and impact to planning and operations · Lead enhancements and changes to Next SCM platform to support D2C operations · Work on back-office integration with NSCM, NERP and D2C Platform · Lead integration of AI technologies into SCM processes, conducting process engineering to identify workflow automation opportunities and deploying agentic AI solutions that improve decision-making and reduce manual effort. · Develop and implement automation and process solutions that enhance operational efficiency and deliver an improved end-to-end customer experience. · D2C Supply and Inventory Management · Ensure weekly planned supply is allocated, received and transferred to Ecommerce Warehouses timely to make the inventory available for sales · Lead supply related conversations with Central SCM and AP2 teams for supply allocation, prioritization on weekly basis · Work with central SCM team and Suwon GOC team for SOP confirmation, getting approvals for exceptions for productions and all other operational planning · Communicate supply lead times for all Estore sub-channels including SMB and other omni-channels and reconcile inventory between sub-channels · Balance and optimize supply between all sub-channels providing deeper insights · Demand Planning analysis for multi-channel inventory · Evaluate demand forecasts across categories and proactively manage supply needs by providing inventory analytics · Evaluate and relocate supply between sub-channels · Approve SOPs, manage emergency supply requests, work with central teams and Suwon office to secure supply Additional responsibilities: · Manage centralized aging across all Ecommerce Inventory · Support buy-box management · Monitor and optimize key supply chain KPIs, identifying and closing gaps between plan and actuals to ensure a smooth, uninterrupted flow of goods through the fulfillment network. · Lead cross-functional collaboration with Central SCM and AP2 teams, Operations, Planning, Logistics, and Product teams to align on shared goals and facilitate execution against revenue targets. · Conduct root cause analysis using Tableau, Excel, and SAP to diagnose execution defects and translate findings into scalable process improvements that prevent recurrence. · Drive cross-functional capacity initiatives and deliver regular program updates — weekly and monthly — to stakeholders including Directors and VPs. Skills and Qualifications Qualifications: · 8-10 years’ experience in Supply Chain Management, Forecasting, Innovation · Bachelor's degree in Supply Chain Management or analytical field; Master’s degree in Supply Chain Management, Analytics/STEM related degree or MBA preferred. · Experience in leading cross functional resources in a matrix organization · Proven experience in inventory management, preferably within the eCommerce or retail industry. · Strong analytical skills with the ability to interpret data and translate into actionable insight with hands-on with advanced excel and Tableau · Excellent communication and collaboration skills to work effectively with cross-functional teams. · Proficiency in inventory management software and ERP systems. · Proficiency of managing Master Data and supply chain system configuration · Hands-on with using agentic AI for supply chain/operations · Knowledge of supply chain best practices and inventory optimization techniques. · Ability to work in a fast-paced environment and manage multiple priorities effectively. · Strong problem-solving skills with a focus on continuous improvement. title: Senior Product Owner
jd_text: Job Seekers can review the Job Applicant Privacy Policy by clicking here . Job Description : SUMMARY The Senior Product Owner, Customer Experience Products, will help lead the strategy, development, and delivery of customer-facing digital products that simplify how customers interact with Ryder services and support organizations. This role is responsible for improving the customer experience through digital self-service, intelligent automation, AI-enabled capabilities, and connected workflows that reduce friction and increase operational efficiency. They will champion both customer and business needs across a complex ecosystem of applications, platforms, and operational processes. Working closely with designers, technologists, operations leaders, and business stakeholders, this role will help define and execute product strategies that improve customer satisfaction, drive digital adoption, and streamline interactions between customers and Ryder teams. The ideal candidate combines strategic thinking with hands-on product execution and is passionate about leveraging emerging technologies to create modern, scalable customer experiences. This role will translate business objectives, customer needs, and operational challenges into product roadmaps, user stories, and measurable outcomes. Success in this position requires strong collaboration, customer empathy, analytical thinking, and the ability to lead cross-functional initiatives in a fast-paced, matrixed environment. ESSENTIAL FUNCTIONS • Customer Service Product Strategy: Define and execute product strategies that improve customer experiences across Ryder's digital ecosystem, including self-service capabilities, customer communications, workflow automation, and operational engagement experiences. • Customer Experience Innovation: Identify opportunities to simplify how customers access information, receive support, complete transactions, and engage with Ryder through digital products. Drive solutions that reduce customer effort while improving transparency and satisfaction. • Automation & AI-Enabled Experiences: Partner with business and technology teams to identify opportunities to leverage automation, artificial intelligence, conversational experiences, predictive insights, and intelligent workflows to improve customer outcomes and operational efficiency. • Omnichannel Customer Engagement: Support the design and delivery of seamless experiences across digital channels including web, mobile, messaging, communications platforms, and future customer engagement technologies, ensuring a consistent and connected customer journey. • Product Delivery & Execution: Lead product discovery, roadmap planning, prioritization, and delivery activities. Translate customer and business needs into product requirements, user stories, and measurable outcomes while partnering closely with technology and delivery teams. • Data-Driven Decision Making: Leverage customer feedback, journey analytics, operational metrics, and product performance data to identify opportunities, prioritize investments, validate outcomes, and continuously improve the experience. • Enterprise Collaboration: Collaborate with business operations, customer experience, technology, data, and commercial teams to align product strategies with enterprise objectives and ensure successful adoption and implementation of product capabilities. ADDITIONAL RESPONSIBILITIES Performs other duties as assigned. EDUCATION Bachelor's degree Business Administration, Supply Chain, Computer Science or equivalent. Master's degree MBA, Supply Chain, Computer Science or equivalent preferred. EXPERIENCE Six (6) years or more experience in product management, digital transformation, solution design, business planning, strategy development, competitive analysis and financial analysis. Eight (8) years or more experience in logistics, operations, engineering, agile development or solution development. Demonstrated experience in new product development preferred. Familiarity with global business practices affecting the supply chain. experience with, or ability to understand, commercial implications of solutions proposed, potential areas of risk and methods to limit liability. experienced in financial business case analysis to help support targeted return on investment. Demonstrated success in assessing, developing and deploying new offerings or incremental enhancements. preferred SKILLS • Experience managing customer-facing digital products focused on self-service, customer engagement, workflow automation, or operational efficiency. • Experience with Artificial Intelligence (AI), Generative AI, conversational experiences, virtual assistants, or intelligent automation solutions. • Experience designing and delivering omnichannel customer experiences across web, mobile, messaging, notifications, and communication platforms. • Experience working with enterprise SaaS platforms, CRM systems, customer engagement platforms, or workflow management solutions. • Experience defining and managing integrations between customer-facing applications and enterprise systems through APIs, middleware, event-driven architectures, or cloud-based integration platforms. • Experience partnering with teams supporting platforms such as Salesforce, service management systems, customer engagement platforms, and enterprise operational applications. • Strong understanding of customer journey mapping, service design, experience measurement, and digital adoption strategies. • Ability to identify opportunities to reduce manual effort, streamline workflows, and improve operational scalability through technology. • Experience defining product success metrics and measuring business outcomes through customer, operational, and financial KPIs. KNOWLEDGE • Knowledge of digital customer experience, customer engagement platforms, SaaS solutions, workflow automation, artificial intelligence, enterprise integrations, and customer service technologies; advanced level preferred. • Knowledge of fleet management or transportation logistics industries; advanced level preferred. TRAVEL 5-10% Job Category Product Development Our Culture & Commitment : At Ryder, you’re trusted to make an impact—while enjoying room to grow and having a voice that’s heard. Our culture is built on respect, collaboration, and shared pride in doing great work rooted in innovation and safety. Your Voice. Your Success. The Future We Build Together. title: Staff Business Systems Analyst – Workday Security & ITGC Lead
jd_text: We're looking for a Staff Business Systems Analyst – Workday Security & ITGC Lead to join Procore's Enterprise Technology and Business Platforms team. In this hands-on technical role, you will be the system administrator and technical owner responsible for Workday security architecture, tenant configurations, business process engineering, and key reporting infrastructure. You aren't just managing compliance on paper—you know Workday inside and out, build and maintain complex configurations, manage service account governance, and ensure system-level changes and business processes adhere to strict security and SOX standards. Reporting to the Sr. Director, Enterprise G&A Technology, this is a deeply technical, hands-on role embedded directly within Enterprise Technology. This role is based in Remote US and we are looking for someone to join us immediately. What You'll Do: Hands-on Workday Configuration & Security: Architect, configure, and maintain Workday security models (domain policies, business process security, constraint groups, segmented security), ensuring system configurations and business process workflows align directly with security and compliance controls. Service Account Governance: Manage and audit all Workday integration system users (ISUs), API service accounts, and elevated access permissions; determine and maintain in-scope service accounts for SOX ITGC and logical access reviews. Key Reporting & Data Integrity: Design, build, and maintain the inventory of Workday Key Reports (IPEs) used in financial and operational controls, utilizing advanced custom reports, calculated fields, and robust change-tracking procedures to guarantee data completeness and accuracy. Technical Change Management: Act as the technical gatekeeper for Workday tenant configuration changes, semi-annual feature updates, and new integrations, ensuring change management standards, SDLC protocols, and testing evidence are strictly executed prior to production deployment. Automated Controls & Job Monitoring: Design, operationalize, and maintain IT Automated Controls (ITACs) and system-enforced validation rules in Workday; monitor critical batch jobs, scheduled processes, integration failures, and ensure documented, timely resolution. Audit Leadership & Evidence Technical Lead: Serve as the primary technical liaison for internal and external audits—independently leading walkthroughs, extracting system logs and security reports directly from Workday, and demonstrating how technical configurations prevent risk. Deficiency Remediation & Systems Rationalization: Perform technical root-cause analysis for any control failures, design technical fix/remediation plans in Workday, validate compensating controls, and drive automated solutions that eliminate manual compliance overhead. AI & Operational Innovation: Apply AI/LLM tooling to streamline systems evidence collection, request triage, and audit documentation while maintaining strict data governance and auditability standards. Cross-Functional & Team Mentorship: Partner closely with Enterprise Integrations, HR Technology, Controllership, and Internal Audit, while mentoring Senior and Associate BSAs on Workday configuration standards and compliance execution. What We're Looking For: 7+ years in business systems analysis, IT systems administration, or IT compliance, with 4+ years of direct, hands-on experience configuring and administering Workday. Deep Workday Technical Expertise: Proven proficiency in configuring Workday Security (domain/BP security policies, ISUs, SoD matrix, security groups) and developing advanced Custom Reports and Calculated Fields for key audit reporting (IPEs). Technical ITGC & Change Management Mastery: Practical experience managing ITGC domains in production environments—logical access provisioning, privileged access reviews, service account management, SDLC/change control, and job scheduling. Demonstrated experience independently leading ITGC and ITAC technical walkthroughs with external audit teams for public companies or SEC registrants. Strong understanding of how business process configurations and tenant settings map to system controls, automated business process validations, and risk mitigation. Proven track record of performing exposure analysis, lookback assessments, and technical remediation for system or process deficiencies. Experience or practical interest in utilizing AI/LLM automation tools for systems operations, data processing, or compliance workflows. Relevant certifications strongly preferred (e.g., Workday Pro Security, Workday Pro Reporting, CISA, CISSP). Additional Information Base Pay Range: 114,912.00 - 158,004.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates: Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

title: Business Systems Lead
jd_text: Whether you’re a recent grad or a seasoned professional, you can experience meaningful career growth at Rosendin. Enjoy a true sense of ownership as you work with a proven industry leader on some of the most exciting and high-profile projects in the nation. We offer a wide range of job opportunities, competitive compensation, full benefits, an Employee Stock Ownership Plan and more. Why Modular Power Solutions (MPS)? COMMITTED. INNOVATIVE. ENGAGED. If you’re looking to take your career to the next level and work with some of the best and brightest in the industry, we want to hear from you. Since our founding, Modular Power Solutions (MPS) has been driven to positively impact the communities where we live and work. We are an organization built on integrity and we have a culture that empowers people, embraces diversity, and inspires everyone to do their best. As one of the largest EMPLOYEE-OWNED electrical contractors in the United States, you will have the unique benefit of being a shareholder at a company that is experiencing tremendous growth and success. When our people succeed and fuel our success, we reward them. We'd love to have you as a shareholder! YOUR NEXT OPPORTUNITY: The Lead, Business Systems is management role that bridges the gap between a company's business needs and technology solutions. This role analyzes current systems, identifies opportunities for improvement, and supports the design and implementation of technology solutions that enhance operational efficiency. The role works closely with business stakeholders and technical teams to gather requirements, document processes, support testing, and enable successful system adoption WHAT YOU’LL DO: Lead and guide a team focused on the technology needs of internal stakeholders. Validate that all labor and material forecasting accurately aligns with production scheduling with different departments to understand business needs, identify pain points, and gather detailed functional requirements for new or improved systems. Lead and support implementation of new systems, including configuration, data migration, and user training. Provide ongoing technical support to users, troubleshooting issues, and answering questions regarding system operations. Analyze system data to identify trends, measure performance, and recommend improvements, scope, timeline, and budget of system development projects. Support and drive the company’s analytics strategy, roadmap, and best practices to ensure data accuracy, completeness, and consistency. Develop dashboards, reports, and KPIs using tools such as Power BI to support business decision-making. Support analytics initiatives by applying statistical and predictive modeling techniques to structured datasets. Ensure data accuracy, consistency, and integrity across systems, reports, and analytics outputs. Communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders to ensure alignment and successful delivery of system initiatives. WHAT YOU’LL NEED TO BE SUCCESSFUL: Proficiency in Microsoft Office tools and experience with enterprise systems such as Oracle or similar platforms. Strong organizational and time management skills, with the ability to prioritize tasks and adapt to changing priorities in a fast-paced environment. Ability to work in a fast-paced environment, manage multiple priorities, and adapt to changing business needs. Strong communication and presentation skills with the ability to collaborate effectively across technical and business teams. Self-motivated and proactive with strong problem-solving and execution skills. Ability to work collaboratively as part of a team, with strong interpersonal skills and the ability to interact effectively with employees at all levels, clients, vendors, and other stakeholders. COMPETENCIES: Strong understanding of MPS business operations, processes, and goals across different departments. Proficiency in ACC and a deep understanding of database structures and data relationships. Expertise in using data visualization tools such as Power BI to transform complex data into meaningful insights. Proven ability to apply statistical and/or machine learning methods to solve business problems, and experience in data modeling and predictive analytics. Strong passion for data, analytics, and continuous learning, with a commitment to staying current on emerging tools, methods, and technologies. Strong critical thinking skills, with the ability to analyze complex data and make strategic recommendations based on insights. WHAT YOU BRING TO US: A bachelor's degree or higher in a quantitative field such as statistics, mathematics, computer science, analytics or related field. 7–10+ years of experience in business systems, analytics, data science, or related operational/technical roles. 5+ years of experience in project or program support, leading workstreams or system initiatives (not full program ownership). Experience working with enterprise systems (e.g., Oracle) and large datasets. TRAVEL: 10-25 % WORKING CONDITIONS: General work environment – sitting for long periods, standing, walking, typing, carrying, pushing, bending. Work is conducted primarily indoors with varying environmental conditions such as fluorescent lighting and air conditioning. Noise level is usually low to medium; it can be loud on the jobsite. We fully comply with the ADA and applicable state law, including considering reasonable accommodation measures that may enable qualified disabled applicants and employees to perform essential functions. The Senior HR Systems Analyst leads configuration changes, supports releases, triages escalations, maintains data integrity, and contributes to Workday governance and continuous improvement. PRINCIPLE RESPONSIBILITIES: Proactively identifies challenges, identifies root cause and designs scalable solutions and system configuration improvements Design and configure complex Workday business processes, condition rules, calculated fields, validations, alerts, notifications, eligibility rules, and EIB templates. Primary owner of complex workstreams and accountable for end-to-end module impacts Responsible for configuration integrity and sustainability Mentors HR Systems Analyst(s) II and serves as an escalation point for complex configuration Provide guidance to Tier 1/Tier 2 HR support teams. Partner with Workday Engineers on technical feasibility and migration processes. Collaborate with Business Analysts to translate requirements into functional design. Partners with product owners, HR leaders, an COEs to consult on HR System needs Maintain configuration documentation, decision logs, and standards. Ensure documentation and controlled migration processes are followed. Performs other job related duties as assigned or apparent. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS: Expertise with Workday business processes, calculated fields, condition rules, EIB, and security fundamentals. Experience with Workday release cycles and regression testing. Must be a self-starter and able to work collaboratively and cooperatively in a team environment Advanced Excel and proficiency with workflow/project tools (Visio, Jira, MS Project, PowerPoint). Strong communication and stakeholder management skills. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: 4 - 7 years of hands-on Workday HRIS experience with deep knowledge of Workday configuration and capabilities within specific modules and the ability to diagnose systems issues to deliver timely solutions to key stakeholders. Candidates must have hands-on experience supporting and administering Workday Time Tracking, Absence, and Payroll modules, with a strong understanding of system configuration, business processes, reporting, and compliance requirements. For any concerns relating to Republic Services’ commitment to equal opportunity employment, you may contact the AWARE Line at 1-866-3-AWARE-4. ABOUT THE COMPANY Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world. In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills. Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer. Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it. Our company values guide our daily actions: Safe : We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities. Committed to Serve : We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations. Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment. Driven : We deliver results in the right way. Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person. We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods. STRATEGY Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets. We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation. With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers. Recycling and Waste We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs. Environmental Solutions Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need. Sustainability Innovation Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth. The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America. Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year). title: Staff Technical Program Manager, Security Engineering
jd_text: We're looking for a Staff Technical Program Manager, Security Engineering to join Procore's Security Engineering organization. In this role, you'll lead the design and execution of large-scale, transformational programs to build and scale an agentic security fleet — an AI-driven, autonomous system that continuously identifies, prioritizes, and remediates threats across Procore's SaaS platform. Your primary goal is to drive the end-to-end delivery of this next-generation security capability, turning complex, ambiguous initiatives into coordinated programs that ship. As a Staff TPM, you'll partner with Security, Product & Technology, IT, and GRC teams to drive alignment, unblock dependencies, and keep the most consequential security programs on track. Use your program leadership, systems thinking, and ability to influence without authority to deliver a security fleet that operates at machine speed and scales with Procore's growth. This is a rare opportunity to shape the security posture of a category-defining construction tech platform from the ground up — apply today. This position reports to the Senior Director, Security Engineering and will be based in our Austin, TX office. We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll do: Lead the program strategy, roadmap, and execution for Procore's agentic security fleet, coordinating work across multiple product, security, and IT teams from inception through production deployment. Define and manage program structure for complex, multi-quarter initiatives — including milestones, dependencies, risks, and escalation paths — ensuring stakeholders have clear visibility at all times. Partner with Security Engineering leadership to translate organizational security priorities into actionable programs with measurable outcomes and delivery timelines. Drive cross-functional alignment across Engineering, Legal, Privacy, and Compliance to ensure the agentic fleet meets regulatory, audit, and enterprise trust requirements. Identify and proactively resolve technical, organizational, and process blockers that impede program delivery, escalating to senior leadership when warranted. Establish and continuously improve program delivery practices, tooling, and rituals for an AI-native security team operating in a fast-moving environment. Communicate program status, risks, and decisions to executive audiences with clarity and confidence, framing technical complexity in terms of business impact. Evaluate and influence architectural and product decisions where program scope, timeline, or quality are at stake. What we're looking for: 8+ years of technical program management experience, with at least 3 years leading large-scale, cross-functional programs in a security, infrastructure, or platform engineering context. Demonstrated experience delivering transformational or greenfield programs — particularly those involving AI/ML systems, autonomous agents, or security automation — from 0 to production. Deep understanding of security engineering concepts (e.g., vulnerability management, detection and response, threat modeling, compliance frameworks) sufficient to engage credibly with senior security engineers and architects. Proven ability to lead through ambiguity, build program structure where none exists, and maintain momentum across distributed teams with competing priorities. Strong executive communication skills — written and verbal — with a track record of synthesizing complex technical programs into crisp, decision-ready updates for leadership. Experience working in or alongside engineering teams, with familiarity with model deployment pipelines, agent frameworks, or autonomous system lifecycle management. Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, or a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience; PMP, CISSP, or equivalent certifications are a plus. A bias for action, high ownership, and the ability to build trust quickly across engineering, product, and security stakeholders in a fast-scaling SaaS environment. Additional Information Base Pay Range: 168,560.00 - 231,770.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. This position requires access to technology, software, and data that is controlled or restricted under U.S. law, regulation, executive order, or government contract. For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates: Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

title: PMO Senior Project Manager
jd_text: Our associates celebrate lives. We celebrate our associates. The Senior Project Manager is responsible for managing a portfolio of complex, large-scale projects spanning one or more areas of the business. This position manages resources, schedules, financials, risks, issues, dependencies, and project change requests while adhering to PMO governance and stage-gate quality control guidelines throughout the full project life cycle. The Senior Project Manager leads projects using traditional, Agile, Scrum, or hybrid delivery approaches based on the needs of the initiative. The role partners with business and technical teams to improve processes, strengthen data quality and governance, support organizational readiness, and ensure projects deliver measurable business outcomes. The Senior Project Manager has the authority to manage assigned projects on a day-to-day basis and verify that each project produces the required deliverables at the expected level of quality, within approved time and cost constraints, and achieves the potential benefits defined in the business case. Job Responsibilities Project & Portfolio Leadership Manage a portfolio of complex, cross-functional projects and programs from initiation through implementation and closure. Partner with business stakeholders to develop project business cases, charters, benefit assumptions, success measures, and project approval documentation. Develop and maintain project plans, budgets, schedules, risk mitigation strategies, and governance processes. Manage project scope, change control, prioritization, and governance processes to ensure alignment with business objectives and approved business cases. Provide leadership and direction to project teams while ensuring alignment with strategic business objectives. Deliver executive-level reporting on milestones, risks, issues, dependencies, financial performance, and project outcomes. Ensure expected business outcomes and benefits are achieved through effective planning, execution, adoption, measurement, and transition to operational ownership. Agile & Scrum Delivery Lead or support projects utilizing Agile, Scrum, Waterfall, or hybrid delivery methodologies. Facilitate Agile planning, prioritization, sprint reviews, retrospectives, and continuous improvement activities. Partner with business and technical teams to manage delivery roadmaps, backlogs, and project priorities. Promote collaboration, accountability, and efficient delivery of business value. Select and apply the most appropriate delivery methodology based on project complexity, stakeholder needs, and organizational objectives. Data Management & Reporting Support data governance, data quality, reporting, and portfolio management initiatives. Develop dashboards, metrics, and reporting tools that provide actionable insights to leadership. Ensure project and portfolio information is maintained accurately within enterprise systems. Identify opportunities to improve data integrity, reporting effectiveness, and decision-making. Analyze trends, performance metrics, and project data to support informed business decisions. Process Improvement & Operational Excellence Lead process improvement initiatives that enhance efficiency, scalability, and business outcomes. Partner with stakeholders to assess current-state processes and implement sustainable improvements. Apply continuous improvement principles to optimize project delivery and operational effectiveness. Support adoption of new processes, tools, and ways of working across the organization. Facilitate process assessments, root cause analysis, and workflow optimization activities. Stakeholder & Vendor Management Build strong relationships with executives, business leaders, technical teams, vendors, and project sponsors. Lead and facilitate project governance, steering committee, executive leadership, and stakeholder meetings to drive decision-making and alignment. Lead vendor evaluation, RFP, demonstration, selection, contracting, implementation, and delivery management activities as required. Collaborate with Change Management resources to support organizational readiness, training, communications, and adoption. Manage stakeholder expectations and ensure alignment between project objectives and business priorities. PMO Leadership Contribute to PMO standards, governance, reporting, methodologies, and best practices. Mentor team members and promote effective project management and Agile delivery techniques. Stay current on emerging project management, Agile, reporting, data management, and process improvement practices. Positively represent and market PMO services across the organization. Support continuous improvement of PMO processes, tools, and service offerings. Minimum Requirements Education Bachelor's degree in Business, Project Management, Information Systems, Data Management, Marketing, or a related field. Build and maintain strong, long-lasting client relationships. Navigate nuances of client relations amongst peers within trusted account relationships. Ability to understand, develop, follow, and enforce standard operating policies and procedures. Ability to perform duties in a professional manner and appearance. Ability to prioritize and manage multiple tasks, changing priorities as necessary. Ability to work under time pressure and adapt to changing requirements with a positive attitude. Effective oral and written communication skills Ability to be self-motivated, proactive and an effective team player. Ability to interact effectively and professionally with all levels of employees, both management and staff alike, vendors, clients, and others WHAT YOU BRING TO US: Bachelor’s Degree in Construction Management, Project Management or other related discipline preferred. Expert knowledge of construction technology, scheduling, Minimum 7 years’ equipment and methods required. Business development/heavy client interaction a plus. jd_text: Our world is transforming, and PTC is leading the way. Our software brings the physical and digital worlds together, enabling companies to improve operations, create better products, and empower people in all aspects of their business. Product Manager – Service Engineering About the Role PTC is seeking a technically strong and market-focused Distinguished Product Manager to lead strategic investments across the Windchill Service Engineering and Arbortext portfolio. This role will define and drive the next generation of PTC’s Service Engineering and Technical Publications solution through the entire Intelligent Product Lifecycle. The ideal candidate combines deep domain expertise in Service Engineering and Technical Publications with strong technical acumen, customer focus, and a passion for applying AI technologies to solve real-world business challenges. Product Focus Areas Windchill Service Information and Service Parts Arbortext Authoring suite & Windchill integrations AI-powered Authoring Content Lifecycle Management and Delivery Your Day-to-Day Define and execute the product vision, strategy, and roadmap for PTC’s Service Information and Arbortext solutions, enabling a connected digital thread across the product lifecycle to meet the needs of Service Engineering, Technical Publications, Service Execution, and Content Delivery. Engage directly with customers, partners, analysts, and field teams to understand business challenges and market opportunities and translate those into effectively roadmap and release plans. Translate business requirements into epics, user stories, and prioritized product backlogs. Engage with R&D teams on technical discussions and provide needed guidance on implementation approaches and backlog execution through product releases activity. Evaluate emerging technologies and identify opportunities to leverage AI and automation. Partner closely with R&D and UX teams to design and deliver innovative and AI powered value driven solutions. Drive Agile planning, backlog management, prioritization, and story acceptance. Support Product launches, Sales enablement, and Go-to-Market activities. Collaborate across Product Management, R&D, Sales, Support and Partners. Technical Skills & Knowledge Required Strong foundation in modern Product Management practices with focus on inbound skills and ability to translate customer needs into successful enterprise solutions. Experience with Agile/Scrum methodologies, backlog management, and user story development. Strong understanding of Product Lifecycle Management (PLM) , Manufacturing Engineering, Service Engineering, Service Lifecycle Management (SLM), Technical Publications. Proven implementation experience in service content workflows of enterprise software applications - structured content, publishing, content delivery etc. Relevant Knowledge of common industry technical documentation standards - DITA 2.0 a must, DITA-OTK, Industry 4.0, S1000D, iiRDS , and eIFUs. Understanding of cloud platforms (Azure, AWS), REST APIs, microservices, and modern SaaS architectures. Familiarity with enterprise search, metadata, taxonomy, and information architecture. Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills. AI & Innovation Focus Strong passion for AI and emerging technologies. Understanding of Generative AI, LLMs, RAG architecture, semantic search, vector databases, knowledge graphs, and AI assistants . Experience identifying and delivering AI-powered customer solutions. Ability to translate AI innovations into product strategy and measurable business value. Knowledge of AI applications for content creation, translation, knowledge management, and service operations. Preferred Experience Windchill, Arbortext, or comparable enterprise platforms. Manufacturing, Aerospace & Defense, Automotive, Industrial Equipment, or Medical Device industries. Service organizations, aftermarket operations, or technical publications teams. Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Engineering, Computer Science, Information Systems, Technical Communication, or a related field. 5+ years of experience in Product Management, Technical Product Management, Engineering, Solution Architecture, or related disciplines. Proven success delivering enterprise software products from concept through market adoption. Demonstrated ability to work effectively with both highly technical teams and executive stakeholders. Success Profile The ideal candidate is a strategic product leader who: bridges business needs and technical implementation. Solves customer problems and delivers great quality product outcomes. is passionate, highly motivated and shapes successful customer implementations drives innovation and critical thinking. influences product strategy across a complex software portfolio. speaks credibly with customers, engineers, service leaders, and executives. title: Critical Operations Manager
jd_text: Who we are: As a global leader in digital infrastructure, QTS designs, builds and operates advanced data centers that support strategic AI, cloud and digital transformation initiatives. We are driven by a mission to connect the world for good and our people make it possible. Every single day, the creativity, dedication and genuine care for our communities are what push us forward and make this a truly special place to be. The Manager, Critical Operations is responsible for the Data Center facility technical strategy, continuous improvement, and development support. This role will support the electrical, mechanical, FLS (Fire, Life, Safety), and DCIM (Data Center Infrastructure management) platforms, and building and housekeeping items from a site operations standpoint. This role will collaborate with the Engineering Manager on technical operations and daily facility needs. This role will own the strategic projects and continuous improvement site items. This leader should have experience with mechanical and electrical data center infrastructure, codes, regulations, required and applied safety standards and practices, as well as data center remote hands and customer support. This role will oversee the teams who perform preventative and corrective maintenance on critical mechanical and electrical equipment. This role will suggest, plan, and implement measures that increase the energy efficiency of the facility. This role requires on-site work hours to support a 24X7X365 data center environment and is not eligible for remote and/or hybrid work. ESSENTIAL DUTIES AND RESPONSIBILITIES - Other duties may be assigned. Maintain, establish, and implement facility policies, procedures and organizational structure within the boundaries established by senior management team and corporate policy while ensuring no contradiction in federal, state, and local operating regulations or laws. Develop and maintain efficient maintenance matrixed operations utilizing maintenance governance, standards utilizing in-house staffing and vendor support to provide 100% up-time of all mechanical, electrical, life safety, monitoring, and control systems. This includes, but is not limited to, developing, and coordinating maintenance agreements, maintenance procedures, testing procedures, inspections, reporting, and accounting practices. Development of emergency response planning, response management and reporting of incident and emergency situations for all mechanical, electrical, associated controls and plumbing systems. Develop, direct, and monitor short-term and long-range business plans consistent with overall profit and growth objectives of the company that establishes operations standards for cost control, waste reduction, quality, safety, and an environmentally friendly community partner. Manage and oversee the execution of building and site cleanliness and preservation operations. Development and management of an effective operating and capital budget. Oversee operations budget to ensure compliance with organizational expenditure requirements. Partner with Development, Sales, Implementation, and Solutions Engineers to deploy and maintain customer environments. Conduct Sales and Customer tours and audits. Ensure the pro-active delivery of corporate services support, power services, COT (Critical Operations Technicians) headcount projections, planning, budgeting, capital projects, maintenance, and business continuity/disaster recovery. Help negotiate improvement project contracts as needed on leased and owned real estate. Confer with professional operations staff subject matter experts (SME’s) to find resolution to operational problems, develop and authorize operational procedures and approve all major estimates. Utilize comparative evaluations between mechanical, electrical, and controls systems performance and key performance indicators to monitor the effectiveness of operational programs through benchmarking and the utilization of best practices. Ensure facilities’ mechanical, electrical, controls, monitoring, and fire-life safety systems compliance with all governmental regulatory operating guidelines. Obtain and keep current all necessary licenses, permits and certifications as required. Supervise, train, develop and coach employees. Works with direct reports to establish performance goals, monitors progress, and advises on ways to enhance their professional development and success. Facilitate Data Center space and cable plant design, implementation, and maintenance. Ensure teams performing equipment installs, managing tickets, communicating, completing tasks pertaining to computer hardware and/or software, and all incidents are resolved in a timely manner. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Seven or more years data center environment or professional equivalent experience. Five or more years people leadership experience in a data center environment. Ability to manage complex situations during off management hours - single point of contact. Strong written, verbal, and interpersonal skills Ability to effectively lead a team environment. The ability to acquire and apply job-related knowledge within set guidelines and expectations. title: Manager, Facilities Operations Commissioning
jd_text: The Manager, Facilities Operations Engineering Commissioning will be responsible for the oversight of commissioning, continuous improvement, and developmental support for sites in a geographic region. This role will provide assistance with commissioning-related engineering, including the coordination, installation, and integration of connectivity, network infrastructure, security, life safety, other building subsystems and finishes, transformers, electrical switchgear, UPS (Uninterrupted Power Supply), STS (Static Transfer Switch), PDU (Power Distribution Unit), electrical distribution equipment, Chillers, water loops/components, Cooling distribution equipment, Electrical Power Monitoring Systems, and Building Management and automation systems. The position requires project planning abilities coupled with leadership through influence and a proactive partnership approach. The ideal candidate will bring experience in electrical and mechanical systems, along with an understanding of large-scale data centers (or comparable environments), which may encompass electrical distribution systems, static UPS, emergency standby generation, fire alarm/suppression, monitoring systems, and cooling systems. This role will be a regional role that reports to the Director, Facility Operations, Commissioning that will require an estimated 30-50% travel to other sites around the U.S. RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned. Manage the commissioning team(s) in assigned region, develop capabilities, engage employees. Follow operating and commissioning standards required for quality, safety, and ongoing operation. Oversee travel budgets to ensure compliance with organizational expenditure requirements. Assist in site construction activity and installations as needed, in coordination with QTS project departments, external construction resources, to ensure system design, installation and testing adhere to operational standards. Direct Cx Engineers to witness testing of all equipment during commissioning in your region and validate sequence of operations and receipt of all operational documentation. Assist Director as necessary in revising comprehensive commissioning plans for Level 1, Level 2, Level 3, Level 4, and Level 5 systems, including connectivity, network infrastructure, security, life safety, other building subsystems and finishes, Electrical, Mechanical, and Building Automation components. Identify, track, and resolve any issues during the commissioning process, working closely with the project team to resolve technical challenges. Utilize findings and provide feedback to program management team to drive continuous improvement. Assist and work with all QTS site teams on standard operating procedures (SOP), method of procedures (MOP), and emergency response procedures (ERP) established for critical environments, as well as the formal change management process. Develop metrics for your team to provide feedback to QTS. Lead your teams in quality improvement, standard compliance, vendor oversight, completions and turnover. Drive innovation into facilities programs/systems with an environmentally conscious attitude. Interfaces with vendors, QTS Engineering, QTS Development and peer operations organizations. Maintain positive relationships and communication with staff and executive level management. Assist site engineering/management with compliance with local health & safety (i.e. OSHA) standards and national electrical and building codes. Ensure proper training and growth of staff. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical or Mechanical Engineering or similar HVAC or critical power certifications OR equivalent professional experience in lieu of degree. Five or more years of direct experience with engineering related activities in a technical or critical environment (data center, nuclear/electric power, hospital, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, industrial/commercial field engineering). PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS Ten or more years of direct experience with engineering related activities in a technical or critical environment (data center, nuclear/electric power, hospital, pharmaceutical, semiconductor, industrial/commercial field engineering). Five or more years of data center engineering, commissioning, project management, or equivalent. Three or more years of management/supervisory experience overseeing engineering or critical operations managers. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES Must be fluent with and possess an excellent working knowledge of Data Center critical and construction environments. Ability to develop solutions and create technical strategic and tactical plans on complex projects. Ability and willingness to think outside of the box to find creative and innovative solutions to improve quality / reliability and continuously drive down operating costs. Advanced understanding of both mechanical and electrical equipment, systems and design related to data centers. (Including but not limited to uninterruptable power sources, diesel generators, electrical switchgear, power distribution units, variable frequency drives, automatic/static transfer switches, chillers (air-cooled and water-cooled), pumps, cooling towers, heat exchangers, CRAHs, air economizers.) Experience with emergency backup systems (generators, UPS, battery backup). Knowledge and experience with building monitoring/controls, electricity and medium / low voltage electrical distribution systems, mechanical systems, telecommunications, access controls, CCTV, life safety systems, and/or building subsystems. Knowledge and experience with project management and commissioning management software systems. Ability to lead multiple Commissioning Teams in various stages of commissioning. TOTAL REWARDS This role is also eligible for a competitive beneﬁts package that includes: medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance; 401(k) retirement plan; ﬂexible spending and HSA accounts; paid holidays; paid time off; paid volunteer days; employee assistance program; tuition assistance; parental leave; military leave assistance; QTS scholarship for dependents; wellness program, and other company beneﬁts. title: Principal Product Manager, Enterprise AI
jd_text: AI is a company-wide priority at Procore. Our leaders are actively engaged, and teams across the business are eager to experiment. Procore exists to improve the lives of everyone in construction, and that starts with our own people: we want Procore to be a place where people do the best work of their careers. AI is a big part of how we'll get there, by putting better tools in everyone's hands, taking routine work off their plates, and freeing up time for more creative and strategic work. To lead that change, we're building a new Enterprise AI Center of Excellence within Procore's Enterprise Technology & Business Platforms team. The team will set the direction for how Procore uses AI across the business, run the programs that bring it to life, and help every team get real value from it. It's a rare chance to build something from the ground up at a company that's serious about AI. We're looking for a Principal Product Manager, Enterprise AI to join the Enterprise AI Center of Excellence. You'll own the strategy and portfolio for AI for operators and builders across the business, meaning how business teams at Procore use and build with AI: which tools and platforms we invest in, which use cases we prioritize, and how we decide. Your goal is to turn AI from a fragmented, team-by-team effort into a coordinated portfolio with clear standards, priorities, and measurable value. This is a business-led technology role, not an infrastructure or engineering position. You'll be the decision owner for enterprise AI tooling. You'll partner with the Principal Architect, Enterprise AI, who leads hands-on technical evaluation, and with AI Platform Engineering, which builds and runs Procore's AI platforms. We’d love for this role to be based in our Austin, Texas office, and we’re open to great candidates anywhere in the U.S. It reports to the Senior Director, Technology Transformation & Enterprise AI. What you'll do Be the product leader for the AI employee experience. Own the roadmap, use case prioritization, adoption strategy, and value delivery for how employees use AI. Own the enterprise AI roadmap and tool portfolio. Decide which AI tools and platforms Procore invests in, how they're sequenced, and when legacy tools are retired. Run tool and platform evaluations. Set the evaluation criteria, weigh business value, cost, and portfolio fit, and make clear recommendations. Partnering with the Principal Architect who leads the technical side of each evaluation. Prioritize the use case portfolio. Score and rank AI use cases from across the business, decide what moves forward and where it's delivered, and stop work that isn't delivering value. Set governance standards. Define how AI tools, connectors, and use cases are evaluated and approved, in partnership with Security, GRC, and Legal. The Staff TPMs, Enterprise AI run the process day to day. Own the shared AI asset library. Treat shared skills, Claude Projects, and agent patterns as a product: decide what goes in, keep it current, and drive reuse across teams. Act as product owner for enterprise agents and Claude. Treat Claude and enterprise-wide agents as internal products: own requirements, priorities, and the roadmap, partnering with AI Platform Engineering on delivery. Define success and show value. Measure AI investments by time to value, productivity improvement, cycle time reduction, employee experience, risk, and financial impact, treating usage as a floor rather than the finish line. Validate realized benefits with business leaders. Work with Analytics and Finance to show what we're getting for what we spend, and shape vendor and license strategy and build-vs-buy recommendations. Bring the business case to leadership. Prepare recommendations for the Enterprise AI SteerCo, keep the portfolio aligned with company priorities, and help hold the boundaries between the Center of Excellence and adjacent teams. What this role doesn't own To keep ownership clear, this role doesn't do hands-on technical evaluation or prototyping (the Principal Architect), run the intake queue (the Staff TPMs, Enterprise AI), own training and adoption programs (the Principal Enablement Manager, Enterprise AI), or build and operate platforms and agents (AI Platform Engineering). What we're looking for 10+ years of product management experience, including leading platform or internal-tools products at enterprise scale Hands-on fluency with generative AI tools and a working understanding of LLMs, agents, and connectors, enough to challenge technical recommendations Demonstrated experience evaluating, selecting, or rolling out AI or automation platforms at enterprise scale, including building business cases with clear cost and value Experience partnering across engineering, data, and business stakeholders to drive adoption of a new technology or platform Strong prioritization judgment across competing stakeholders, and comfort saying no Comfortable operating in ambiguity and building structure where none currently exists Technically credible while staying focused on business outcomes, and commercially minded about value realization, not technology deployment alone Proven ability to influence across organizational boundaries without direct authority Experience partnering with security, legal, and compliance teams on governance Clear communication with executives, business leaders, and engineers Additional Information Base Pay Range: 198,240.00 - 272,580.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates: Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

title: Senior Finance Analyst - M&A Integration
jd_text: We’re looking for a Senior Finance Analyst - M&A Integration to join Procore’s Finance Transformation Team. In this role, you will serve as the primary engine for post-close value realization, ensuring acquired companies are seamlessly folded into the Procore ecosystem and deal theses are converted into tangible operational and financial results. Your primary goal is to drive the successful integration of acquired businesses by coordinating cross-functional execution, tracking synergy capture, and ensuring strategic and financial objectives are fully realized. As a Senior Finance Analyst - M&A Integration , you’ll partner with Finance, HR, IT, Legal, and Operations stakeholders to lead end-to-end post-acquisition workstreams from Day 1 readiness through full synergy realization. Use your financial systems proficiency, analytical rigor, and project management discipline to bridge the gap between deal strategy and operational reality while mitigating integration risks for leadership. This high-impact role puts you at the absolute center of Procore's growth strategy, offering direct visibility into how deals are valued, executed, and transformed into scalable business results—apply today! This position reports into the VP - Finance Transformation & Technology and will be based in our Austin, TX office or remote. We’re looking for someone to join us immediately. What you’ll do: Lead the end-to-end execution of post-acquisition Finance integration workstreams, managing processes from Day 1 readiness through full operational synergy capture. title: Architect, Enterprise Data
jd_text: We're looking for an Architect, Enterprise Data to join Procore's Enterprise Data Engineering team. In this role, you'll be a force multiplier for the business: designing and building the data platform that puts trusted data directly in the hands of stakeholders so they can make faster, better decisions. AI is central to that mission, and you'll lead how we use it to help every team do more with their data. As an Architect, Enterprise Data , you'll own the end-to-end architecture of our enterprise data platform, spanning ingestion, warehousing, analytics, data science/ML, and AI agents. This is a hands-on individual contributor role: you'll author the architecture and also write the code, build reference implementations, and create the self-service tools and patterns that let both engineers and business teams unlock business outcomes faster using data. You'll partner with technical and business leaders across the company and lead the data platform side of mergers and acquisitions. This position reports to the Director, Enterprise Data Engineering and will be based in our Austin, TX office . What you'll do Own the end-to-end architecture of Procore's enterprise data platform across ingestion, warehousing, analytics, data science/ML, and reverse ETL designed so business stakeholders can get from question to trusted answer quickly Lead the platform AI strategy for enterprise data, enabling us to build agents and natural-language interfaces that let business users explore data, automate routine analysis, and move from insight to action Build self-service capabilities, including a governed semantic layer and certified data sources, that put data directly in the hands of business teams and reduce dependence on engineering Act as a force multiplier by creating reusable patterns, templates, and golden paths that help engineers and analysts across the company deliver more Contribute hands-on to building the platform: write production code, build proofs of concept, and prove out new approaches before scaling them Own the data platform strategy for M&A, from assessing acquired companies' data landscapes to leading integration into the enterprise platform Establish standards for data quality, testing, governance, observability, and cost efficiency so stakeholders can trust and act on the data, partnering with Security and Legal on privacy and compliance Partner with Enterprise Technology, Enterprise Analytics & Reporting, and business leaders to shape the data platform roadmap around business outcomes, and provide technical leadership to senior engineers through design reviews and mentorship (this role has no direct reports) What we're looking for 15+ years of experience in data engineering, data architecture, or software engineering, including significant time architecting enterprise-scale data platforms Deep hands-on experience with Snowflake and/or Databricks, including performance tuning, cost optimization, and security model design Strong proficiency in SQL and Python, and hands-on experience with Fivetran, dbt, Airflow, and Census (or similar tools) Proven track record in data warehouse development, including dimensional modeling and building governed data models and semantic layers A track record of enabling self-service analytics and increasing data adoption among non-technical business users, with measurable impact on decision speed or business outcomes Experience building and shipping AI/LLM-powered applications or agents that business users adopt (e.g., Databricks Genie), plus experience supporting ML workloads Experience leading data integration for M&A or other large-scale platform consolidations Demonstrated ability to lead senior engineers and align technical and business stakeholders without direct authority, with excellent communication skills Additional Information Base Pay title: Manager, Data Engineering & Analytics
jd_text: About the Role We are looking for a Manager, Data Engineering & Analytics to own the architecture, delivery, and evolution of our enterprise data platform. This is a hybrid leadership and hands-on role: you’ll manage a team of data engineers while staying close to the data modeling, pipeline architecture, and business automation work that keeps the platform running. You will act as the bridge between business stakeholders and technical execution — scoping requirements, architecting scalable solutions in Google BigQuery and dbt, orchestrating integrations through SnapLogic, and overseeing our Tableau environment. Responsibilities Team Leadership & Agile Delivery Manage and mentor a team of data engineers, providing regular feedback, technical coaching, performance reviews, and career development support. Own the team’s Jira board and lead Agile/Scrum ceremonies, including backlog grooming, sprint planning, task estimation, and delivery tracking. Build a culture of technical excellence, accountability, clear documentation, and continuous learning. Data Architecture, Engineering & Business Automation Architect and maintain our data transformation layer in dbt, ensuring modular, tested, and well-documented data models. Manage and optimize our enterprise data warehouse in Google BigQuery, including performance tuning, cost management, and access controls. Build and monitor ELT pipelines and automated workflows using SnapLogic and REST APIs to connect core SaaS platforms and enterprise systems. Design and run proof-of-concepts to evaluate emerging technologies and architectural enhancements. Platform Administration & Governance Administer Tableau, including server/site governance, user permissions, licensing, performance monitoring, and content promotion. Establish and champion best practices for data modeling, version control (Git), CI/CD, and technical documentation. Ensure data integrity, reliability, and security compliance across all ingestion and reporting layers. Business Partnership & Stakeholder Engagement Partner directly with cross-functional business leaders to translate strategy into technical data roadmaps and actionable user stories. Coordinate User Acceptance Testing (UAT) and validate data deliverables alongside business partners. Maintain SOPs and data dictionaries to drive data literacy across the organization. Qualifications Required: 5+ years in Data Engineering, Analytics Engineering, or Enterprise Data Solutions. 2+ years of formal people management, or demonstrated experience leading engineering squads, sprint planning, and managing backlogs in Jira. Production-level experience designing, optimizing, and managing a cloud data warehouse (Google BigQuery or Snowflake preferred). Advanced dbt experience — architecting and deploying projects using macros, tests, incremental models, and documentation. Hands-on experience building integrations using an enterprise iPaaS (e.g., SnapLogic, Workato, Fivetran, Boomi) and third-party REST APIs. Hands-on experience administering a modern BI platform (Tableau user management, data sources, and site administration preferred). Proven ability to communicate technical trade-offs to non-technical business partners and document complex, end-to-end data workflows. Preferred: Experience with Python or another scripting language for data pipelines and automation. Certifications such as dbt Certified Developer, GCP Professional Data Engineer, or Tableau Certified Administrator. Background in data governance and security compliance frameworks (SOC 2, GDPR) and data quality monitoring. Experience integrating AI/LLM tools into data workflows — e.g., connecting platforms via Model Context Protocol (MCP), or building with Claude/Gemini APIs for automation, documentation, or analytics use cases. What You’ll Bring A strong sense of ownership across both the technical roadmap and the people delivering it. Comfort operating at the intersection of platform architecture, integration engineering, and BI administration. The judgment to know when to be hands-on and when to delegate, coach, and let the team lead. A collaborative, documentation-first mindset that scales knowledge beyond any one person. Why Join Us You’ll shape the next stage of our data platform — from warehouse architecture to the integrations and dashboards the business relies on every day — while building and growing a team around you. Plan for Success First 30 Days: Team Integration & Operational Takeover During your first month, you will focus on integrating with the team, building relationships, and establishing an operational rhythm. People Leadership: Take ownership of conducting regular 1:1 meetings with your direct reports and begin leading the team's twice-weekly stand-up sessions. Operational Management: Assume responsibility for sprint planning directly from the work backlog and map out existing team workflows. Technical Familiarization: Begin a deep dive into learning the team's current technology and tool stack. First 60 Days: Stakeholder Engagement & Tool Fluency By the second month, you will expand your scope to own external alignment and solidify your technical foundation. Stakeholder Management: Take ownership of leading stakeholder engagement and requirements gathering for incoming projects. Technical Proficiency: Achieve a strong, practical working knowledge of the team’s entire tool stack to effectively guide technical execution. First 90 Days: Strategic Contribution By the end of your first quarter, you will transition from day-to-day execution to driving long-term impact. Strategic Roadmap: Move beyond daily operations to contribute directly to the team's strategic direction and process improvements. End-to-End Ownership: Fully own the stakeholder relationship and project lifecycle from initial intake to final delivery. Benefits and Compensation listed vary based on the location of your employment and the nature of your employment with SailPoint. As a part of the total compensation package, this role may be eligible for the SailPoint Corporate Bonus Plan or a role-specific commission, along with potential eligibility for equity participation. SailPoint maintains broad salary ranges for its roles to account for variations in knowledge, skills, experience, market conditions and locations, as well as reflect SailPoint’s differing products, industries, and lines of business. Candidates are typically placed into the range based on the preceding factors as well as internal peer equity. We estimate the base salary, for US-based employees, will be in this range from (min-max, USD): $104,500 - $176,174.00 Base salaries for employees based in other locations are competitive for the employee’s home location. Life protection: Life insurance and Accidental Death & Dismemberment (AD&D) 4. Additional life coverage options: Supplemental life insurance for employees, spouses, and children 5. Flexible spending accounts for health care, and dependent care; limited purpose flexible spending account 6. Financial security: 401(k) Savings and Investment Plan with company matching 7. Time off benefits: Flexible vacation policy 8. Holidays: 8 paid holidays annually 9. Sick leave 10. Parental support: Paid parental leave 11. Employee Assistance Program (EAP) and Care Counselors 12. Voluntary benefits: Legal Assistance, Critical Illness, Accident, Hospital Indemnity and Pet Insurance options 13. Health Savings Account (HSA) with employer contribution SailPoint is an equal opportunity employer and we welcome all qualified candidates to apply to join our team.
