title: Senior Solutions Architect, Field Deployments - DroneDeploy
jd_text: DroneDeploy, the robotics and visual intelligence platform for the built world that is used on over 3 million jobsites across more than 180 countries, is now a part of Procore Technologies Inc., the global provider of construction management software. As a leader in reality capture and robotic automation, DroneDeploy delivers the visual intelligence that bridges the built world—from active construction sites to operational assets—and the digital world, providing critical, real-time visibility into daily operations. Procore Technologies is the leading technology partner for every stage of construction. We empower construction teams to drive efficiency and mitigate risk through actionable AI & data-driven insights. For over 20 years, we have been transforming the industry with purpose-built solutions for construction professionals and we’re looking for talented people to help us build together. We are looking for a Senior Solutions Architect, Field Deployments to serve as a trusted technical advisor across the customer lifecycle, helping customers design, validate, and deploy solutions that solve real-world operational challenges. As the Senior Solution Architect on our Solutions Engineering team, you will work closely with Sales, Customer Success, Product, Engineering, and cross-functional partners to translate business goals, field constraints, and technical requirements into scalable solutions. Your strengths in consultative technical discovery, robotics/hardware systems integration, and cross-functional solution architecture will drive your success. Run demonstrations, proof of concepts, and validation activities for complex customer opportunities. Act as the primary technical advisor, clearly communicating risks, tradeoffs, recommendations, and next steps to customer stakeholders. Architect scalable solutions that align customer needs with product capabilities, implementation requirements, and long-term business value. Partner with Product and Engineering to define, test, and improve emerging workflows across robotics, walkthrough AI, and reality capture. Bring structured field feedback directly into product roadmap discussions to drive adoption, reliability, and solution quality. Use AI tooling regularly to support research, solution design, technical content creation, and workflow documentation. What You Bring 8+ years of experience in solutions architecture, solutions engineering, systems engineering, technical consulting, or a similar customer-facing technical role. Background in ground robotics, quadrupeds, mobile robots, or embodied AI systems. Proficiency with Python, ROS, or similar tools used in robotics and automation integration. title: Sr. Lead Engineer, Integration & Automation
jd_text: Ready to be a Titan? ServiceTitan's Finance Business Technology team is seeking a Sr Lead engineer , Integration & Automations to serve as the technical cornerstone of our integration and automation practice. This is a newly created role designed to elevate the maturity, reliability, and strategic impact of our integration estate across Finance, Revenue, Billing, People Technology, and Go-to-Market. You will own the end-to-end technical vision for how our enterprise systems connect - spanning Workday Financials, Workday HCM, Workato, Salesforce, and a growing ecosystem of SaaS platforms. You will set and enforce engineering standards, lead architecture reviews, and serve as the primary technical partner to senior Finance, HR, and GTM stakeholders. You will also partner with and technically guide a cross-functional team of integration engineers and automation specialists across US and India-based pods. This role is equal parts architect, technical lead, and team enabler. You will report directly to the Director of G&A Systems and play a central role in driving our AI and Automation goals. What you'll do: Technical Leadership & Architecture Define and maintain the integration architecture across Finance, Revenue, People Tech, and Go-to-Market domains, ensuring designs are scalable, secure, and aligned with enterprise standards Author and enforce integration design guidelines, coding standards, SLAs, and tiering frameworks based on business criticality - including patterns for error handling, idempotency, retry logic, and alerting Lead architecture reviews for all net-new integrations and significant enhancements across the team's functional pods; own the final technical design decision on high-complexity builds Evaluate and recommend tools, platforms, and integration patterns to support the evolving roadmap; assess build-vs-configure tradeoffs across iPaaS, native connectors, and custom API development Conduct an audit of the current integration estate, identify technical debt and failure-prone patterns, and build and execute a prioritized hardening roadmap Define and evolve the integration tier model - classifying integrations by business criticality and enforcing appropriate monitoring, SLA, and change management standards for each tier Hands-On Engineering Optimize and maintain complex integrations in Workday Studio (EIB, Core Connectors, Document Transformation, XSLT) and Workato, including net-new builds and major refactors of existing integrations Develop reusable integration components, transformation templates, and shared libraries that reduce build time and enforce consistency across the team Build and maintain API-based integrations connecting Workday, Salesforce, Snowflake, Avalara, Workato, and other platforms using REST/SOAP, JSON/XML, OAuth, and event-driven patterns Own integration monitoring and alerting - instrumenting integrations with proactive health checks and ensuring failures surface before stakeholders notice them Perform deep root cause analysis on critical integration failures; produce post-incident documentation and implement systemic fixes to prevent recurrence Team Leadership & Development Partner with the Manager to recruit, onboard, and develop integration talent across US and India-based pods Run Integration & Automation grooming sessions - the biweekly stakeholder-facing forum where new integration requests are triaged, scoped, and sized before entering the cross-functional prioritization process Serve as the L3 escalation point for integration incidents across all pods; ensure root cause analysis and preventive follow-up are completed for all critical failures Foster a culture of documentation, runbook discipline, and knowledge sharing across onshore and offshore team members Automation Program Partner with the Manager to drive the AI and automation delivery pipeline, ensuring the backlog is continuously groomed and prioritized by impact Identify and champion high-value automation opportunities surfaced through stakeholder grooming sessions and the automation initiative pipeline Ensure all automation solutions are production-grade - monitored, documented, and resilient to upstream system changes Stakeholder Engagement Serve as the senior technical point of contact for Finance, People Tech, Revenue, Billing, and GTM stakeholders on integration-related matters Translate complex integration and architecture concepts into clear, business-relevant communication for non-technical audiences Participate in the Cross-Functional Prioritization Meeting, providing architectural input and capacity guidance to inform sprint planning What you'll bring: 8+ years of experience in enterprise integration engineering, systems architecture, or a senior integration role Proven hands-on experience with Workato or a comparable iPaaS platform (MuleSoft, Boomi, Informatica); able to design, build, and maintain complex multi-step recipes and error-handling workflows independently Hands-on expertise in Workday Studio - including EIB, Core Connectors, Document Transformation, and XSLT; ability to build and troubleshoot complex Studio integrations without vendor support Strong command of integration architecture patterns: REST and SOAP API design, event-driven and pub/sub architecture, data transformation, idempotency, retry and dead-letter handling Experience building API integrations against Salesforce (REST/Bulk API), Workday, Snowflake, or similar platforms; comfort reading and writing JSON, XML, and XSLT Demonstrated experience leading technical teams including offshore or distributed engineers; able to set the technical bar, conduct design reviews, and develop engineers below you Experience building or maturing integration governance frameworks - tiering models, design standards, SLA frameworks, and monitoring and alerting practices Ability to independently audit an integration estate, produce a prioritized technical debt roadmap, and execute against it Excellent written and verbal communication skills; equally comfortable in a design review with engineers and a planning conversation with senior Finance or HR leaders Experience working in a SaaS or high-growth technology company where agility and cross-functional collaboration are the norm Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field; equivalent experience considered NICE TO HAVE Workday certification in Studio, Financials, or HCM Experience with Salesforce integrations in a Revenue or Billing context, including CPQ or Salesforce Billing data flows Familiarity with SQL and Snowflake for validating data flows, debugging transformation logic, and supporting Finance analytics use cases Exposure to SOX-compliant integration environments and the documentation and audit requirements associated with them Experience building out a greenfield integration practice or leading a team through a significant maturity uplift Familiarity with Workday Orchestrate or event-driven automation patterns within the Workday platform Be Human With Us: Being human isn’t about checking every box on a list. It’s about the experiences we have, people we meet, and the perspectives we share. So, if you have the skills but are hesitant to apply because of your background, apply anyway. We need amazing people like you to help us challenge the conventional and think differently about the problems that we’re solving. We’re in this together. Come be human, with us. Use of AI Technology: We use technology, including automated and AI-assisted tools, to support certain aspects of our recruitment process. These tools are designed to improve efficiency and enhance the candidate experience. AI tools are not used to make hiring decisions; all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. What We Offer: When you join our team, you’re not just accepting a job. You’re making a career move. Here’s how we’ll support you in doing some of the most impactful work of your career: Flextime, recognition, and support for autonomous work : Flexible time off with ample learning and development opportunities to continue growing your career. We offer a comprehensive onboarding program, leadership training for Titans at all levels, and other programs and events. Great work is rewarded through Bonusly, peer-nominated awards, and more. title: Presales Solutions Architect - Enterprise Networking
jd_text: About Us Since 1989, SHI International Corp. has helped organizations change the world through technology. We’ve grown every year since, and today we’re proud to be a $16 billion global provider of IT solutions and services. Over 17,000 organizations worldwide rely on SHI’s concierge approach to help them solve what’s next. But the heartbeat of SHI is our employees – all 7,000 of them. If you join our team, you’ll enjoy: Our commitment to diversity, as the largest minority- and woman-owned enterprise in the U.S. Continuous professional growth and leadership opportunities. Health, wellness, and financial benefits to offer peace of mind to you and your family. World-class facilities and the technology you need to thrive – in our offices or yours. Job Summary The Presales Solutions Architect – Enterprise Networking at SHI International is responsible for being SHI's Subject Matter Expert across the enterprise networking domain. The foundation of this role is core networking – routing and switching, campus LAN architecture, and WAN and SD-WAN design – with working breadth across enterprise wireless, network access control and segmentation, network management and observability, and network automation. We are looking for depth in core networking first. Candidates who bring strong routing, switching, and WAN architecture experience and can speak credibly to the adjacent domains are encouraged to apply, even if their hands-on depth is uneven across every area listed below. In this role, you will split your time between presales client engagements and internal practice development. On the presales side, you'll take a consultative approach, leading technical discovery sessions with clients to assess their network infrastructure maturity, designing target-state enterprise network architectures, and delivering compelling demos, POCs, and technical presentations. On the internal side, you'll build reusable collateral such as reference architectures, battle cards, and enablement content; evaluate and qualify new vendor partnerships; and conduct training sessions that keep our engineering and sales teams current on emerging network technologies, platform capabilities, and best practices. Your credibility and technical depth will make you a trusted advisor to both SHI's most strategic customers and our internal stakeholders, driving meaningful network outcomes and revenue growth across the Networking practice. title: Senior Product Manager -  Data and AI Platform
jd_text: Ready to be a Titan? At ServiceTitan, we're building the operating system for the trades. As we continue to scale, we're looking for a Senior Product Manager to join our Data & AI Platform team and own the algorithmic systems that sit underneath dozens of downstream product features and quietly decide what gets prioritized, surfaced, and trusted across ServiceTitan. This is a senior individual contributor role for a product leader who thinks in statistics, not just user stories. The specific problems you'll own will shift based on what domain teams and our customers need most — today that might mean ranking methodology, deduplication logic, or causal inference; tomorrow it could be a different statistically-driven problem entirely. What stays constant is the kind of thinking: translating ambiguous, statistically messy problems into clear product requirements that engineering and ML can build against with confidence. This is a heavily stats-driven PM role: you'll be evaluating model tradeoffs, defining what "correct" means for a given system, and defending methodology choices to a technical audience as much as you'll be writing a roadmap. What you'll do: Define and own the roadmap for whichever algorithmic systems — ranking, deduplication, causal inference, or similar — are highest-priority based on domain team and customer need. Translate real customer pain (bad matches, untrustworthy rankings, wrong conclusions drawn from correlated data) into statistically rigorous product requirements. Co-author PRDs for statistically ambiguous problems where the "right answer" isn't obvious — you're defining the evaluation criteria as much as the solution. Partner with ML and engineering to evaluate model tradeoffs (precision/recall, false positive cost, explainability vs. accuracy) and make the product call when there's no clean answer. Set measurable, multi-quarter goals for algorithmic system health and lead cross-functional teams toward them with rigor. Lead discovery with domain product teams and customers to understand where algorithmic errors actually cost time, money, or trust. Proactively identify and resolve disagreements over methodology, ownership, and model quality before they stall multiple teams building on your systems. What you'll bring: 5+ years of product management experience, strong track record in enterprise B2B SaaS; experience with at least one of ranking/recommendation systems, entity resolution, or causal inference — this role will likely touch more than one over time. Genuine statistical fluency — comfortable with precision/recall tradeoffs, confounding vs. causation, and model evaluation, regardless of which specific problem you're applied to. Demonstrated ability to define evaluation criteria and "what correct looks like" for a new statistical problem from scratch, rather than working from an existing rubric. Comfort context-switching between different algorithmic domains as customer and business priorities shift. Experience translating customer-reported problems (bad matches, low trust in recommendations, wrong conclusions) into statistically defined product work. Strong communication skills — explaining model tradeoffs to domain PMs, ML engineers, and customers who each need a different level of technical detail. Self-starter who takes initiative and holds themselves accountable to outcomes — "mostly works" isn't good enough when customers are trusting your systems with real decisions. Bachelors degree in Computer Science, or equivalent work experience. Why This Role Matters: Ranking, deduplication, causal inference — and whatever comes next — quietly decide what ServiceTitan surfaces, trusts, and acts on, for both internal teams and the customers depending on those systems being right. Get it wrong, and the failure isn't loud — it's a customer trusting a bad recommendation, or two records that should've been merged staying separate. Your job is to bring statistical rigor to decisions most PMs never have to make, driven by what domain teams and customers actually need, not a fixed technical checklist. Be Human With Us: Being human isn’t about checking every box on a list. It’s about the experiences we have, people we meet, and the perspectives we share. So, if you have the skills but are hesitant to apply because of your background, apply anyway. We need amazing people like you to help us challenge the conventional and think differently about the problems that we’re solving. We’re in this together. Come be human, with us. Use of AI Technology: We use technology, including automated and AI-assisted tools, to support certain aspects of our recruitment process. These tools are designed to improve efficiency and enhance the candidate experience. AI tools are not used to make hiring decisions; all hiring decisions are made by our hiring teams. What We Offer: When you join our team, you’re not just accepting a job. You’re making a career move. Here’s how we’ll support you in doing some of the most impactful work of your career: Flextime, recognition, and support for autonomous work : Flexible time off with ample learning and development opportunities to continue growing your career. We offer a comprehensive onboarding program, leadership training for Titans at all levels, and other programs and events. Great work is rewarded through Bonusly, peer-nominated awards, and more. Holistic health and wellness benefits: Company-paid medical, dental, and vision (with 100% employer paid options and 90% coverage for dependents), FSA and HSA, 401k match, and telehealth options including memberships to One Medical. Support for Titans at all stages of life: Parental leave and support, up to $20k in fertility services (i.e. IUI and IVF), surrogacy, and adoption reimbursement, on demand maternity support through Maven Maternity, free breast milk shipping through Maven Milk, pet insurance, legal advisory services, financial planning tools, and more. At ServiceTitan, we celebrate individuality and uniqueness. We believe that the convergence of fresh perspectives and experiences from all walks of life is what makes our product and culture so great. title: Capital Equipment Procurement Manager - Electrical
jd_text: The Capital Equipment Procurement Manager is responsible for planning, budgeting, strategic sourcing, supply chain management, critical supplier performance management and stakeholder management for their critical OFCI equipment in the electrical category . This role will be responsible to develop long-term business strategies aligned with key QTS stakeholders, executives, and other Procurement leaders to drive results directly linked to the business goals that contribute to QTS’s position as a leader in the market. This role requires a strategic thinker with strong negotiation skills, an in-depth understanding of HVAC systems, and the ability to manage supplier relationships effectively. As a Capital Equipment Procurement Manager in the mechanical category, you will report to the Director, Capital Equipment Procurement for electrical equipment. RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned. Analyze capital plans to drill down equipment and services required to establish OFCI equipment budget and rolling 12-month procurement plans accounting for and adjusting to the sales projection updates. Ensure accurate cost and schedules are provided in a timely manner to the Development Program Managers in support of budget approvals and project schedule planning. Provide weekly Development procurement status, progresses, and recommendations to gain support from executives to align on the business objectives. Continually evaluate new critical infrastructure technologies with partners to ensure that QTS balances cost, availability, reliability and efficiency into its standard equipment offering. Analyze category spend management opportunities, conducts research to understand the supply market and commodity trends, and deploy appropriate strategic plans and track KPI’s. Ensure QTS policies and processes are followed and continuously improve processes and systems to drive best-in-class procurement performance. Collaborate with Global Procurement leaders to ensure alignment and execution of category strategies. Continuously identify and implement strategies to improve procurement initiatives, increase speed to market, improve quality, and achieve a lower total cost of ownership. Understand business impacts and align with stakeholders to effectively assess risk levels, manage supply continuity, develop contingency plans, and establish risk management strategies to mitigate risk. Lead ongoing category management activities within assigned scope of spend categories to achieve business objectives and benefit targets. Develop RFP packages and lead competitive sourcing events to ensure structuring of commercial value, risk mitigation, and performances requirements are secured in a contract to protect QTS’s interests. Support Sales revenue generator by securing competitive NRC costing for customer deals as requested. Solicit and develop construction related contracts to support QTS projects and associated timelines. Monitor market supply chain conditions and anticipate needs of various project to ensure ordering of OFCI equipment for just-in-time delivery to meet QTS timelines. Resolve unforeseen technical and commercial issues that arise from the assigned projects, engage with subject matter experts, and escalate as necessary to close processes utilizing approved corrective actions. Ensure the most up to date design standards are distributed to the OFCI suppliers to deliver the products as specified. Obtain OFCI equipment submittals to support the design, specification, and process approval for each assigned project as needed. Track and manage equipment inventory locations to analyze and recommend action plan to prioritize reallocation of capital assets to achieve cost avoidance when possible. Develop KPIs to measure supplier performance (on-site delivery performance, cost savings, etc.) Ensure mutual contracted obligations to ensure the negotiated values are realized. Lead periodic business reviews (such as weekly meetings, QBRs, problem resolution, etc.) Consult with QTS Site Operations teams, Suppliers, Finance etc. to be the escalation point on issues and lead process improvement initiatives to drive efficiency and maximize value. Travel to QTS sites, OEM facilities, trade conferences, and networking events to facilitate strong relationships to benefit the strategic positioning of QTS and department objectives. Provide ad-hoc assistance to the Site Operations’ needs on certain difficult to source equipment, parts, and services. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business Administration, Management, Operations, Finance, certificate in Construction Management, or equivalent experience Five or more years of relevant experience in Sourcing / Procurement / Project Management / Engineering Experience developing long range sourcing plans for assigned categories to reduce total costs, optimize value from suppliers, and meet internal customer requirements. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 5 or more years direct experience in global supply chain management, project management, category management, strategic sourcing, electrical engineering, and negotiations, and vendor management in variety of categories Data center or critical infrastructure industry experience including Facility Management, Critical Electrical and Mechanical Equipment, Construction Design and Construction, and Professional Services Experience in leading change initiatives involving significant impacts to organization. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES Ability to resolve conflicts and solve problems. Skilled in building relationships with key stakeholders to gather category requirements, specifications from departments, and category subject matter experts. title: Capital Equipment Procurement Manager - Power Generation
jd_text: Capital Equipment Procurement Manager – Onsite Power Generation Locations: Irving, TX Richmond, VA Overland Park, Kansas The Capital Equipment Procurement Manager – Onsite Power Generation is responsible for planning, budgeting, strategic sourcing, supply chain management, supplier performance, supply chain resilience / risk management, and stakeholder alignment for QTS onsite power generation equipment and related services. This role will support QTS’s Energy Innovation, Utilities Delivery, Development, Finance, Legal, and Facility Operations teams by managing procurement activity for mobile and stationary generation solutions, including gas turbines, reciprocating engines, fuel cells, generator step-up transformers, SCR/emissions systems, generator balance-of-plant, BESS and related power infrastructure, fuel supply, virtual pipeline services, fleet management, and temporary/bridging power services. The role requires a commercially focused procurement leader who can build supplier strategies, manage long-lead equipment risk, negotiate complex commercial structures, and help QTS secure reliable, scalable, and cost-effective onsite power capacity to support accelerated campus development. As a Capital Equipment Procurement Manager in the Onsite Power Generation category, you will report to the Senior Manager, Capital Equipment Procurement for power generation equipment and services. RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned. Analyze QTS power generation capital plans to define equipment, services, and long-lead needs for onsite generation, including mobile turbines, stationary turbines, reciprocating engines, fuel cells, BESS, GSUs, SCRs, fuel systems, and balance-of-plant scope. Provide timely and accurate cost, lead-time, logistics, commercial-risk, and schedule inputs Energy Innovation, Utilities Delivery, Development, Finance, Legal, and Facility Operations teams to support capital approvals, project schedules, customer commitments, and power availability milestones. Provide weekly procurement status updates for active onsite generation workstreams, including supplier commitments, manufacturing progress, permitting or emissions-related dependencies, delivery risk, commercial exposure, and recommended executive decisions. Evaluate new and existing onsite power technologies with internal partners, including gas turbines, medium-speed reciprocating engines, fuel cells, BESS, generator packages, emissions control systems, and alternative fuel solutions, to balance speed to market, reliability, cost, emissions requirements, and operational flexibility. Analyze category spend, supplier capacity, commodity exposure, warranty structures, escalation risk, manufacturing slot availability, and market trends across power generation OEMs, balance-of-plant providers, fuel suppliers, temporary power providers, and service partners. Ensure QTS policies and processes are followed and continuously improve processes and systems to drive best-in-class procurement performance. Collaborate with Global Procurement leaders to ensure alignment and execution of category strategies. Continuously identify and implement strategies to improve procurement initiatives, increase speed to market, improve quality, and achieve a lower total cost of ownership. Understand business impacts and align with stakeholders to effectively assess risk levels, manage supply continuity, develop contingency plans, and establish risk management strategies to mitigate risk. Lead ongoing category management activities within assigned scope of spend categories to achieve business objectives and benefit targets. Develop RFIs, RFPs, term sheets, bid forms, and commercial recommendation packages for onsite power generation equipment and services, ensuring pricing, scope, schedule, liquidated damages, warranties, performance requirements, emissions obligations, spare parts, service support, and risk allocation are clearly defined before award. Support revenue and campus development opportunities by securing competitive, schedule-aligned power generation cost inputs for customer deals, bridging power solutions, and long-term onsite generation strategies. Solicit and develop agreements for power generation-related services, including fleet management, operations and maintenance support, commissioning support, temporary power, fuel supply, virtual pipeline services, installation support, testing, and specialty engineering services needed to support QTS project timelines. Monitor supplier capacity, manufacturing schedules, logistics constraints, permitting dependencies, emissions equipment availability, fuel infrastructure readiness, and project demand to ensure timely ordering and delivery of onsite power generation equipment and services. Resolve technical and commercial issues that arise during sourcing, contracting, manufacturing, factory testing, delivery, installation, commissioning, and turnover of power generation assets; engage Engineering, Development, Facility Operations, Legal, Finance, and supplier subject matter experts as needed. Ensure suppliers have current QTS technical standards, campus requirements, interface requirements, emissions expectations, fuel assumptions, controls requirements, testing requirements, documentation standards, and project-specific specifications before production or service execution. Obtain and coordinate supplier submittals, technical exceptions, commercial clarifications, factory test plans, quality documentation, commissioning documentation, spare parts recommendations, schedule updates, and closeout packages for assigned onsite power generation projects. Track and manage generation equipment inventory, reserved production slots, spare parts, transformers, major auxiliaries, and mobile fleet assets to support reallocation decisions, cost avoidance, schedule recovery, and strategic deployment across QTS campuses. Develop KPIs to measure supplier performance, including on-time delivery, manufacturing milestone adherence, commercial responsiveness, submittal quality, warranty responsiveness, commissioning support, service availability, and total cost performance. Ensure mutual contracted obligations to ensure the negotiated values are realized. Lead periodic business reviews with OEMs, fleet operators, fuel providers, EPC or installation partners, and service providers to review safety, quality, schedule, cost, technical performance, warranty, continuous improvement, and future capacity needs. Serve as an escalation point between suppliers and internal stakeholders to resolve issues and improve end-to-end procurement execution. Travel to QTS sites, OEM facilities, trade conferences, and networking events to facilitate strong relationships to benefit the strategic positioning of QTS and department objectives. Provide ad-hoc support to Site Operations and project teams for difficult-to-source generation parts, emergency power needs, fuel supply constraints, service support, field modifications, warranty claims, and supplier escalations. BASIC QUALIFICATIONS Bachelor’s degree in Procurement, Supply Chain Management, Engineering, Business Administration, Management, Operations, Finance, certificate in Construction Management, or equivalent experience Five or more years of relevant experience in strategic sourcing, procurement, project management, engineering, construction, operations, or supplier management supporting power generation, energy infrastructure, utility infrastructure, data centers, industrial facilities, or other mission-critical environments. Experience developing long-range sourcing plans, supplier strategies, commercial recommendations, and risk mitigation plans for complex equipment or services with long lead times, high capital value, and cross-functional stakeholder impact. PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS 8 or more years of direct experience in global supply chain management, project management, category management, strategic sourcing, engineering, negotiations, and vendor management supporting power generation, energy infrastructure, gas turbines, generators, fuel cells, BESS, utility-scale electrical equipment, or critical-facility infrastructure. Data center, utility, independent power producer, EPC, OEM, or critical infrastructure experience with onsite generation systems, backup generation, temporary or mobile power, emissions control, generator step-up transformers, fuel supply, commissioning, and operations support. Working knowledge of commercial risks associated with power generation procurement, including production slot reservations, escalation clauses, cancellation terms, LDs, warranty coverage, performance guarantees, spare parts, service agreements, emissions compliance, fuel availability, logistics, and commissioning support. Experience in leading change initiatives involving significant impacts to organization. KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS, AND ABILITIES Ability to resolve conflicts and solve problems across technical, commercial, schedule, and field-execution issues involving high-value power generation equipment and services. Skilled in building relationships with suppliers, internal and external stakeholders to gather requirements and drive alignment. Business relationship management Influencing and persuasion skills Strong strategic analysis skills with the ability to connect supplier capacity, market pricing, generation technology, fuel strategy, emissions requirements, project schedule, and total cost of ownership into actionable procurement recommendations. Ability to manage complexity across multiple power generation workstreams, campuses, suppliers, technologies, and internal stakeholders while maintaining clear priorities, risk visibility, and execution discipline. Ability to facilitate collaboration and focus organization on exceeding targets. People motivation and development expertise Change management. Commercial fluency in power generation procurement, including supplier negotiations, equipment reservation strategies, capital approval support, scope definition, contract compliance, change management, and supplier performance management. TOTAL REWARDS This role is also eligible for a competitive benefits package that includes medical, dental, vision, life, and disability insurance; 401(k) retirement plan; flexible spending and HSA accounts; paid holidays; paid time off; paid volunteer days; employee assistance program; tuition assistance; parental leave; military leave assistance; QTS scholarship for dependents; wellness program, and other company benefits. title: Global Partner Program Manager
jd_text: We’re looking for a Global Partner Program Manager to join Procore’s Partner Strategy & Ops Organization. In this role, you’ll design, optimize, and govern our global partner ecosystem architecture, spanning segmentation, economic modeling, and incentive strategy. Your primary goal will be to build a scalable, profitable, and competitive partner framework that drives measurable business value for both Procore and our partners. As a Global Partner Program Manager, you’ll partner with Sales, Finance, Legal, RevOps, Enablement, and Marketing to establish partner tiering, structure discount models, and align cross-functional governance. Use your financial acumen, analytical expertise, and strategic vision to optimize partner profitability, drive ecosystem growth, and deliver high-impact program refreshes. Join a dynamic team building the foundation of Procore’s global channel engine—apply today! This position reports into the VP of Channel Partners and can be based remotely in the US, with Austin, TX preferred. We’re looking for someone to join us immediately. What you’ll do: Define partner segmentation and build comprehensive tiering frameworks, establishing clear requirements, criteria, and benefits across all partner types. Structure partner discount models by type and tier, conducting continuous profitability modeling and cost-to-serve analysis. Design and implement partner-facing incentives alongside internal sales representative compensation models to maximize ecosystem ROI. Manage MDF and incentive budgets, accurately forecasting program costs and analyzing acquisition economics across partner channels. Establish and govern global program terms, policies, and operational guidelines to maintain consistency and compliance. Lead comprehensive annual program refreshes and drive cross-functional change management initiatives across the global organization. Conduct competitive program benchmarking to ensure Procore maintains a highly attractive, market-leading partner proposition. Collaborate with Revenue Operations and Finance to maintain program metrics, reporting, and dashboard tracking via Salesforce and PRM platforms. What we’re looking for: Bachelor’s degree or equivalent practical work experience. 6+ years of experience in partner program design, channel strategy, or partner operations within a B2B SaaS environment. Deep financial acumen with hands-on experience in partner profitability modeling, CAC analysis, and MDF budget sizing. Strong technical and analytical proficiency with SQL, Python, Tableau, Salesforce, and PRM platforms. Proven track record of designing partner tiering architectures, discount structures, and internal/external incentive models. Demonstrated ability to lead corporate governance, program policy enforcement, and cross-functional change management. Excellent cross-functional leadership skills with a proven track record of influencing partners across Sales, Finance, Legal, RevOps, and Marketing. Builder mentality with a data-driven approach, strong commercial acumen, and a growth mindset. Additional Information Base Pay Range: 129,600.00 - 178,200.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates: Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

title: Lifecycle Operations Manager
jd_text: COMPANY 🌱 RYZE was founded in 2019 by Andrée Werner and Rashad Hossain, out of a parents' basement 🏠, with a mission to change daily health, starting with the morning routine: a nutrient-dense mushroom coffee ☕🍄 delivering clean energy ⚡, mental clarity 🧠, and immune support 🛡️. Built on a Direct-to-Consumer foundation with a performance marketing engine, RYZE achieved hockey-stick growth 📈 and a community of over 1 million active subscribers. 🎉 DTC remains the foundation, but RYZE has expanded into mass retail 🛒, quickly becoming the #2 item in Target's overall coffee category and is now executing a multi-channel expansion, with a cross-category launch coming in early 2027 🚀. RYZE is uniquely positioned to redefine how people think about daily wellness. ✨ We're a lean, fast-moving, mission-driven team who believe daily rituals create the foundation for living your greatest life, and we're just getting started! 🌱🔥 WHAT YOU'LL DO 🎯 We're looking for a Lifecycle Operations Manager to sit at the intersection of marketing strategy and technical execution — the person who takes lifecycle briefs and journey maps and turns them into live, tested, working flows in Klaviyo and Postscript. This is not a campaign coordinator role. This is the technical half of the lifecycle partnership: the person who interrogates the brief, surfaces the gaps, builds the logic layer, and keeps the stack healthy. You build things that work — and you know what it takes to keep them working. Responsibilities will include: Translate Strategy into Built Experiences Take lifecycle briefs, journey maps, and campaign strategy and turn them into robust, tested, live flows in Klaviyo and Postscript — built and scheduled, not near-final drafts. Interrogate the brief before you build it: surface gaps a strategist wouldn't think to specify — customers already in the flow, active subscribers, recent sends, no order history. Tell Marketing when something isn't buildable as written — and come back with the version that is, or the work required to make it possible. Configure the full logic layer: triggers, filters, conditional splits, profile property conditions, wait timing, smart sending, and suppression. Coordinate email and SMS so channels complement rather than collide, and build the guardrails and governance that keep sending rules consistent as the program grows. Build the Foundation That Makes It Possible Own the technical health of our lifecycle stack — Klaviyo, Postscript, Shopify, and Recharge — including integration stability, data governance, and documentation that outlives any one person's memory. Own the tracking layer end to end: verify that Shopify, Recharge, and on-site events land in Klaviyo with the right properties, on the right profile, at the right time. If Marketing wants to trigger on something we don't currently capture, you make it capturable. Configure and troubleshoot webhooks, API-driven events, custom metrics, and profile properties. Maintain source-of-truth definitions for the events, attributes, and segments the retention program runs on. Drive operational efficiency by building reusable systems — modular templates, universal content blocks, dynamic content logic — so the tenth version of a journey takes a fraction of the time the first one did. Lead the evaluation and onboarding of new capabilities with a clear view of impact vs. complexity. Test It and Launch It Own the pre-send QA standard for every email and SMS build: dynamic content and personalization across edge cases, link and UTM accuracy, alt text, dark mode, mobile, and rendering across major inbox clients. QA the technical side of landing pages: form and popup behavior, consent capture, list assignment, redirects, mobile rendering, and whether tracking actually fires. QA product and subscription configuration: variants, selling plans, discount and bundle logic, Recharge subscription rules, one-time vs. recurring behavior, and swap or upsell flows. Operationalize A/B tests end to end: audience configuration, randomization, holdouts, and instrumentation that's actually measurable. Help define clear experiment frameworks — success metrics, sample sizes, timelines — and make sure the implementation is technically sound so results mean something. Keep It Running Monitor flow health, delivery, and errors proactively. Broken things should surface on your dashboard, not in a post-mortem. Find and fix silent failures before they become reporting problems: events that stopped firing, properties that drifted, duplicate or mis-identified profiles, integrations that quietly desynced. Monitor sending health — bounce and complaint rates, list growth quality, suppression hygiene, sunset logic — and keep authentication and sending domain configuration in good standing. Own reporting requirements for lifecycle ops: flow health, delivery and error monitoring, and experiment status. Proactively consolidate or retire journeys that add operational complexity without adding return. WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR 🔍 2–4 years of hands-on experience in lifecycle / CRM operations at a DTC or ecommerce brand, working directly from marketing briefs. Deep working knowledge of Klaviyo as your primary tool — flows, segments, templates, and integrations, not just campaign sends. Hands-on experience with Shopify and Recharge, including how subscription data behaves and where it tends to break. Experience with an SMS platform — Postscript preferred; Attentive, Klaviyo SMS, or similar considered. Technical proficiency with HTML, CSS for email, and templating logic (Liquid or similar); comfortable reading, writing, and debugging dynamic content and personalization rules. Demonstrated experience partnering with developers or data teams on integrations, event tracking, and troubleshooting. You can read an API doc, test an endpoint, and reason about a webhook payload without hand-holding. Solid understanding of experiment design — control vs. test, holdouts, key metrics, avoiding bias — and its practical constraints in a live sending program. Proven ability to manage multiple builds in parallel with clear prioritization and communication — and to tell a stakeholder what's realistic before committing to it. PERSONAL CHARACTERISTICS 💫 Low-ego, team-first: The best idea wins, no matter whose it is Self-starter: You see what needs doing and get after it, no waiting for direction Comfortable in ambiguity: Fast pace and shifting priorities energize you rather than rattle you Builder at heart: You're energized by a fast-moving environment where you help create the processes and playbooks, not just follow them Mission-driven: You genuinely care about wellness and are excited to help build RYZE's next chapter WHAT WE OFFER 🌟 Benefits Competitive hourly or monthly contract compensation 💰 Fully remote, flexible work environment 🌍 Opportunity to work on high-impact performance creative for a fast-growing brand 🚀 Access to RYZE creative assets, tools, templates, and performance insights 🎨

title: Senior Manager, Customs Compliance Operations
jd_text: Position Summary Headquartered in Plano, Texas, Samsung Electronics America, Inc. (SEA) is a leader in mobile technologies, consumer electronics, home appliances and enterprise solutions. From our humble beginnings to our position today as a tech leader, our passion for innovation has been the common thread throughout our history. We’ve grown into one of THE most recognized global brands. We consider ourselves “relentless pioneers” that push boundaries and defy barriers. The company pushes beyond the limits of today’s technology to provide groundbreaking connected experiences across its large portfolio of products and services, including mobile devices, home appliances, home entertainment, 5G networks, and digital displays. As EPA’s ENERGY STAR® Corporate Commitment Partner, SEA is dedicated to making a positive impact on the environment through its eco-conscious products, practices, and operations. Role and Responsibilities Responsibilities Hands-on day-to-day import, export, and logistics activity (e.g., review of transport documents, tariff designation, provide broker instructions). Leverage internal tools to designate Product Import classification of finished product and service parts (USHTS) and ECCN codes, maintain data management in the company ERP, and issue parts database. Coordinate and conduct import audits (e.g., Tariff Code, value, quantity, FTA Claims) and monitor Brokerage compliance through Metrics and Broker Scorecards. Ensure the designated Customs Broker maintains compliance and exercises reasonable care in filing Samsung customs declarations, whether they are consumption or foreign trade zone entries. Audit (e.g., accuracy of import data and billing rates) and process vendor billing invoices. Monitor and assess impact of local and global customs changes and related laws and regulations, ability to summarize and provide guidance to mitigate risk (e.g., Section 301, USITC litigation cases, Forced Labor, Trade Modernization, Supply Chain Security, etc.) Support the development of SOPs and training and the refinement and implementation of Trade Compliance-related processes and Best Practices. Assist the Logistics department and Finance/Accounting in analyzing costs for duties and taxes, international transportation and develop methods to minimize or reduce costs. Support the export function, document creation, guidance, direction, and restricted party screening activities when necessary. Assist in internal company global policies and finance audits. Support with cross-functional projects related to trade transactions. Minimum Qualifications Bachelor’s Degree in Business, International Trade or equivalent experience. Minimum 6 years of International Trade experience with a good understanding of core trade principles (e.g., valuation, tariff coding, free trade agreements, reconciliation, etc.). Knowledge of Microsoft Office products (e.g., Excel, PowerPoint, and Word). undefined Preferred Qualifications License Customs Broker, preferable but not required. Critical Thinking and Analytical skills with respect to data manipulation, and the ability to create actionable and informative data (e.g., Alteryx, Tableau, dashboarding). A high level of confidence, integrity, enthusiasm, and executive presence fits a fast-paced, energetic, and proactive organization. Experience working with Telecom, Technology, Consumer Electronics, or Retail industry. title: Warehouse Automation Maintenance Manager
jd_text: Job Seekers can review the Job Applicant Privacy Policy by clicking here . Job Description : We are hiring a Warehouse Automation Maintenance Manager in Lancaster, TX to support our Supply Chain Solutions division. Apply here today to speak with a Recruiter about the position and perks of joining our Ryder Ever Better Team. Pay Type: Exempt / Salary paid Twice Per Month Annual Salary Pay: $110,000-$115,000+ based on experience W arehouse automation maintenance leadership experience required In this role you will: Lead a team responsible for maintaining and maximizing uptime of advanced automated warehouse equipment, including LGV/AGV systems, conveyors, and related automation technologies in a high-volume distribution environment. Bring strong diagnostic and troubleshooting skills in industrial electrical and mechanical systems, including reading schematics, tracing wiring issues, and using diagnostic tools such as multimeters. Serve as a hands-on leader who partners closely with technicians, audits work quality, drives preventive maintenance initiatives, and supports continuous improvement efforts. Thrive in a fast-paced by communicating effectively with customers and site leadership by providing clear updates, presenting maintenance performance metrics, and leading issue resolution efforts. Contribute to the operational success of a 24/7 automated operation by combining strong organization, technical expertise, and a collaborative leadership style to ensure equipment reliability. When Fortune 500 businesses and new startups need supply chain solutions, they look to our industry-leading logistics experts. At Ryder, there is more to being a supply chain professional than working on some of the nation’s biggest brands. We make sure you are also getting the diverse experience, advancement opportunities, all from an industry-leading Fortune 500 company. Here are a few of the many benefits when working with us: Medical, Dental, Vision Benefits start at 30 Days 401 (K) Savings Plan with a company match Discounted employee stock purchase options Quality employee discounts that actually save you money on tools, cars, appliances, travel and more All major holidays paid and Paid time off within your first year Up to 12 weeks paid maternity leave Apply Here With Ryder Today We want YOU to join our family made up of Proud Women and Men in Logistics who work alongside Military Reserve and Veterans we hire every day! Click here to see all Opportunities at Ryder: https://ryder.com/careers EEO/AA/Female/Minority/Disabled/Veteran Summary The Automation Maintenance Manager is responsible for the management and execution of a comprehensive maintenance program for their assigned business unit for both automation and facilities. This position ensures that the business’ key maintenance objectives, plans and strategies are effectively communicated and implemented within their respective business unit. This role will oversee hourly maintenance employees and will function as a subject matter expert and lead the performance, reliability, and continuous improvement of autonomous vehicle systems (AGVs/LGVs) in a highly automated distribution center. Essential Functions Works to implement strategies key to business, customer and site performance measurement developed by leadership in conjunction with onsite CI processes. Monitor AGV software platforms and integrations with WES/WCS systems for optimized vehicle traffic and task efficiency. Manage day-to-day performance and health of AGV/LGV systems including uptime, fault response, and battery diagnostics. Ensure all equipment and automation is at solution up time. Basic cost tracking of spare parts and vendor costs. Manage performance of direct reports to include LGV Technicians and LGV Fault Chasers (also referred to as “Wranglers”). Track/minimize staff OT. Must complete basic planning for PMs and typical repair projects for a specific site/sites. This includes day-to-day troubleshooting and repair, as well as identifying and driving continuous improvement initiatives and fostering accountability. Assist in the Implementation of business maintenance programs. Assist in directing the maintenance activities including policy compliance, marketing and sales support. This includes the monitoring of KPI’s that has been set up previously, MTF, vendor response, along with other critical items needed to support optimal automation performance. Lead the calibration and alignment of AGV systems (e.g., LIDAR, encoders, navigation sensors, drive units). Generate and present detailed equipment health reports, downtime trends, and maintenance KPIs. Manage teams internally to ensure the best result at the most cost-effective solution. Conduct root cause analysis (RCA) on recurring faults or systemic issues; implement corrective and preventive actions. Adhere to maintenance strategies. Perform and manage preventative maintenance functions of team on lower, to mid complexity automated sites. Additional Responsibilities Perform other duties as requested. Skills and Abilities Ability to create and maintain professional relationships within all levels of the organization (peers, work groups, customers, supervisors)., Required Able to manage multiple internal/external customers through their team to achieve required timelines., Required Demonstrated ability to read, analyze, and interpret operation manuals, operating and maintenance instructions, blueprints, etc., Required Must be a critical problem solver and know how to escalate issues outside the 4 walls., Required Qualifications H.S. Diploma/GED, Required Bachelor's Degree in business, Logistics, Engineering, or related field., Preferred 3 years or more in maintenance management experience while supervising others, Required 5 years or more in automation/mechanical maintenance, Required Electrical (including high voltage systems) and mechanical equipment, conveyance systems and warehouse automation. Advanced, Required Background in managing vendors. Advanced, Required Experience using and in trouble-shooting automation control issues using Warehouse Control Systems (WCS) or Warehouse Execution Systems (WES) or advanced PLC troubleshooting. Advanced, Required Experience maintaining spare parts inventories and Preventive Maintenance schedules using a Computerized Maintenance Management System (CMMS). Advanced, Required Basic proficiency in MS Excel and maintenance software. Beginner, Required Travel Yes, 0-10% DOT Regulated No #INDexempt #LI-RK Job Category Logistics Our Culture & Commitment : At Ryder, you’re trusted to make an impact—while enjoying room to grow and having a voice that’s heard. Our culture is built on respect, collaboration, and shared pride in doing great work rooted in innovation and safety. Your Voice. Your Success. The Future We Build Together. title: Sr. Manager, Fulfillment Performance and Optimization
jd_text: Position Summary This role is not eligible for immigration sponsorship Samsung Electronics America, Inc. (SEA), the U.S. Sales and Marketing subsidiary, is a leader in mobile technologies, consumer electronics, home appliances, enterprise solutions and networks systems. For more than four decades, Samsung has driven innovation, economic growth and workforce opportunity across the United States—investing over $100 billion and employing more than 20,000 people nationwide. By integrating our large portfolio of products, services and AI technology, we’re creating smarter, sustainable and more connected experiences that empower people to live better. SEA is a wholly owned subsidiary of Samsung Electronics Co., Ltd. To learn more, visit Samsung.com. For the latest news, visit news.samsung.com/us. Role and Responsibilities Delivering large, complex products to customers’ homes is among the more demanding problems in eCommerce. It spans multiple partners, fulfillment pathways, and systems. Performance is measured daily in cost, service, and customer experience. Samsung Electronics America is seeking a Sr. Manager, eCommerce Fulfillment Performance and Optimization to own the economic model of fulfillment performance. The job of this role is to translate operational performance, carrier results, and customer feedback into quantified cost. That model drives how volume is allocated across our carrier network, which operational priorities the organization pursues, and how platform investment is directed. The ideal candidate brings deep expertise in quantitative decision modeling, cost-to-serve analysis, and operational performance measurement, with experience turning complex data into decisions that move a large operation. This individual will work cross-functionally with Fulfillment Operations, and the broader logistics organization to optimize how our fulfillment network performs across cost and service. This is an analytical and modeling role, rather than a reporting or day-to-day operations role. Based in our Plano, TX office, this position carries visibility to senior leadership and significant influence over how our fulfillment network performs. Specific responsibilities include: Performance measurement and cost modeling: Own the Cost of Poor Quality (COPQ) model, converting service outcomes, damages, returns, reschedules, and customer contacts into quantified cost by driver. Partner with Data and Analytics Team to define the measurement framework for delivery promise accuracy, root cause attribution, and fulfillment path performance. Own metric definitions and attribution methodology across Fulfillment Operations. Quantify comparative performance across fulfillment paths, carriers, markets, product categories, and service levels Establish and maintain promise attainment measurement against the original customer commitment, consistent with standard supply chain reference definitions. Carrier and fulfillment path optimization: Own the analytical models behind carrier allocation strategy, including cost-to-serve normalization across paths with differing cost structures. Recommend allocation configuration changes, supported by simulation against order history, and measure realized impact following implementation. Optimize allocation within contractual volume commitments, rate tiers, and additional continually-evolving constraints. Model the cost and service profile of prospective fulfillment network changes ahead of commitment, and track the performance against that model afterward. Improvement Agenda: Maintain a single prioritized, dollar-sized view of performance drivers across all fulfillment paths and domains. Bring root cause, quantified impact, and supporting evidence to the accountable domain owner. Track initiatives to closure and verify results in the data. Validate that implemented improvements hold by verifying realized impact against the original case, and refreshing cost coefficients on a set cadence to keep the models current. Lead a recurring fulfillment performance review with cross-functional domain owners. Platform roadmap and initiative economics: Build the analytical case behind platform enhancement requests, including ROI quantification for market requirements documents. Model proposed service and pricing initiatives ahead of commitment. Ensure operational remediation, revenue generating, and cost saving initiatives are quantified on one consistent economic basis. Validate realized impact after launch and feed results back into the model. Skills and Qualifications Minimum Qualifications: Bachelor’s degree required. 8+ years of relevant experience in analytical, operations, or commercial roles, with meaningful exposure to physical operations or logistics. Demonstrated ownership of cost or service performance outcomes in an operational environment. Proven ability to build quantitative decision models, and to defend the methodology and assumptions behind them. Experience translating complex analysis into executive-level recommendations and driving decisions from it. Strong cross-functional presence, with the ability to hold credibility among both operational leaders and technical teams. Preferred Qualifications: Experience in supply chain, logistics, fulfillment, or eCommerce operations. Direct experience with operations excellence, quality engineering, or continuous improvement (DMAIC, cost of quality) Direct experience with appointment-based delivery and installation logistics. Background in pricing, revenue management, or another discipline requiring quantified trade-off analysis. Advanced degree in Analytics, Supply Chain, Engineering, or a related quantitative field. title: Senior Counsel, M&A Integration
jd_text: We’re looking for a Senior Counsel, M&A Integration to join Procore’s Legal, Regulatory & Compliance (LRC) Department. In this new role, you’ll serve as the primary legal architect for LRC’s post-acquisition success, orchestrating the end-to-end legal integration of acquired companies into the Procore ecosystem. The primary goal of this role is to lead the legal integration of Procore's acquisitions, ensuring a successful and seamless transition aligned with our global legal standards. As a Senior Counsel, M&A Integration, you’ll partner closely with cross-functional teams including Corporate Strategy, Corporate Development, Product & Technology, Revenue Operations, Sales, Security, People, and Finance, and teams within LRC across the Corporate, Commercial, Product, Privacy, Compliance, and Legal Operations functions, to drive LRC’s integration strategy and execution. You will use your deep legal and subject matter expertise, project management mastery, and AI-first mindset to accelerate time-to-value for our acquisitions while mitigating and managing associated risks. This role is an exciting new position that will play an important role in Procore’s continued growth and success, and offers significant LRC and senior leadership-level visibility in driving LRC’s integration strategy for the company’s highest priority initiatives. We are looking for a high-impact leader who views M&A integration not just as a checklist, but as a strategic lever for Procore’s global growth. This position reports to Procore’s Senior Director & Assistant General Counsel, Sales and can be based in Procore’s Austin, TX office or one of our other U.S.-based offices, or for the right candidate may be remote. We’re looking for someone to join us immediately. What you’ll do: Lead the Legal Lifecycle: Project manage the end-to-end legal integration of acquired entities, coordinating across functional leads in go-to-market, commercial terms, operations, systems, product, privacy, compliance, and IP to ensure alignment with Procore standards. Drive Integration Strategy: Partner with Corporate Development during due diligence to identify integration risks early and influence the overarching integration roadmap, including participation in executive outreach. Cross-Functional Orchestration: Serve as the central legal point of contact and connective tissue between the Commercial Legal team and specialized functions like Privacy, Security, Product Legal, and Finance, ensuring integration milestones are met. Executive Navigation: Facilitate executive outreach and provide clear, predictive updates on integration milestones and potential blockers to leadership. Commercial Alignment: Partner with the Commercial Legal team to streamline the transition of acquired customer and vendor contracts, ensuring a unified go-to-market motion post-close aligned with Procore’s standard practices. Process Innovation: Develop and scale repeatable legal integration playbooks, processes, and templates that leverage Procore’s AI-driven tools to increase deal velocity and ensure a consistent integration motion. AI Thought Leadership: Provide thought leadership on AI utilization to transform M&A integration strategies, establishing scalable, tech-forward processes that accelerate timelines and improve efficiency. Risk Mitigation: Proactively identify and communicate legal risks associated with the transition of people, processes, and technology during the integration lifecycle, and remediate compliance gaps within acquired product suites, particularly regarding data residency and global privacy standards. What we’re looking for: J.D. and active State Bar membership in good standing. Proven Track Record: 10+ years of relevant experience, including demonstrated expertise in M&A integration, legal operations, and complex commercial legal motions, gained at a nationally prominent law firm(s) and in-house legal department(s) (ideally at a SaaS or other high-growth technology company) in roles of increasing responsibility. Commercial & Privacy Expertise: Extensive experience in complex SaaS and other commercial technology transactions and a strong understanding of global privacy laws as they relate to SaaS and other commercial technology agreements. Tech-Forward Mindset: A forward-thinking, AI-first mindset with a passion for exploring and implementing innovative AI strategies that optimize M&A integration by driving efficiency and delivering greater value. Experience in leveraging AI solutions, such as Google Gemini, NotebookLM, and Harvey, a strong plus. Change Management Expertise: Experience orchestrating the operational transition for acquired sales teams by designing legal enablement strategies; driving the adoption of unified operating and transactional models, and ensuring seamless integration of acquired entities through cross-functional stakeholder alignment and continuous process optimization. Agile Problem Solver: Highly resilient and tenacious; able to navigate ambiguity, manage shifting priorities, and deliver results amidst unpredictable challenges and high-pressure timelines. Strategic Playbook Design: Proven ability to architect commercial integration frameworks, harmonizing divergent risk appetites, negotiation postures, and operational motions into a streamlined, unified go-to-market strategy. Exceptional Communicator: The ability to translate complex legal concepts into actionable business advice that resonates with stakeholders at all levels, with a passion for educating and thought-partnering with others. Operational Excellence: Detail-oriented with exceptional project management skills and a passion for process improvement—you don’t just follow a process, you build a better one. Unwavering Integrity: Exceptional business acumen, judgment, and discretion in dealing with highly sensitive information. Collaborative Influence: Outstanding interpersonal skills and demonstrated ability to identify and collaborate with key stakeholders, influence without direct authority, and interface effectively with all business functions and levels to drive business initiatives across global, decentralized teams. Proficiency with Google Workspace (including Slides, Sheets, Docs, and Drive), project management applications (including Airtable), Slack, Salesforce, and Ironclad a strong plus. Additional Information Base Pay Range: 200,000.00 - 275,000.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. For Los Angeles County (unincorporated) Candidates: Procore will consider for employment all qualified applicants, including those with arrest or conviction records, in accordance with the requirements of applicable federal, state, and local laws, including the City of Los Angeles’ Fair Chance Initiative for Hiring Ordinance, the Los Angeles County Fair Chance Ordinance for Employers, and the California Fair Chance Act. A criminal history may have a direct, adverse, and negative relationship on the following job duties, potentially resulting in the withdrawal of the conditional offer of employment: 1. appropriately managing, accessing, and handling confidential information including proprietary and trade secret information, as well as accessing Procore's information technology systems and platforms; 2. interacting with and occasionally having unsupervised contact with internal/external customers, stakeholders, and/or colleagues; and 3. exercising sound judgment.

title: Emerging Technology Architect
jd_text: As passionate about our people as we are about our mission. Why Join Q2? Q2 is a leading provider of digital banking and lending solutions to banks, credit unions, alternative finance companies, and fintechs in the U.S. and internationally. Our mission is simple: build strong and diverse communities through innovative financial technology—and we do that by empowering our people to help create success for our customers. What Makes Q2 Special? Being as passionate about our people as we are about our mission. We celebrate our employees in many ways through our year-round Q2 ChangeMakers awards program and global moments of recognition and connection. We invest in the growth and development of our team members through ongoing learning opportunities, internal mobility, and meaningful leadership relationships. We also know that nothing builds trust and collaboration like having fun and giving back together. From company-wide volunteer days to events like our Q2 Homecoming Week—featuring learning, community service, and culture-building experiences—we create opportunities to connect, grow, and make an impact. The Emerging Technology Architect designs and evolves enterprise AI systems and architectures that enable scalable, secure, and high-impact adoption across the organization. This role defines end-to-end AI solution patterns involving large language models, APIs, retrieval-augmented generation, vector search, intelligent agents, orchestration workflows, Snowflake, cloud platforms such as AWS and Azure, and enterprise data integration. The role partners across data, engineering, business applications, operations, identity and access management, and governance teams to create reusable frameworks that accelerate delivery while supporting security, access controls, compliance, and audit needs. This position may require minimal travel for collaboration, planning, or stakeholder engagement. A Typical Day: Design enterprise AI solution patterns that align business needs with scalable, secure, and maintainable implementation approaches. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to translate complex business challenges into structured architecture recommendations. Identify, analyze, and resolve gaps related to scalability, data readiness, interoperability, and operational adoption of AI systems. Define reusable frameworks and standards that improve delivery consistency and accelerate adoption across teams and use cases. Evaluate solution options, assess trade-offs, and provide recommendations that balance performance, cost, risk, and business value. Guide teams through architecture decisions that support responsible AI adoption and long-term maintainability. Influence organizational direction by promoting best practices, shared patterns, and practical governance approaches across engineering and business teams. Stay current on emerging AI and enterprise technology practices and assess their applicability to organizational priorities. Bring Your Passion, Do What You Love. Here’s What We’re Looking For: Typically requires a Bachelor’s degree in (relevant degree) and a minimum of 12 years of related experience; or an advanced degree with 8+ years of experience; or equivalent related work experience. Strong understanding of enterprise architecture principles, system design, integration patterns, and scalable delivery models. Demonstrated experience with AI and machine learning technologies including large language models, retrieval-augmented generation, vector databases, intelligent agents, and cloud-based AI platforms (AWS, Azure, or equivalent). Experience partnering with business and technical stakeholders to define practical solutions for complex organizational needs. Ability to evaluate ambiguous problems, structure recommendations, and communicate trade-offs clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences. Demonstrated judgment in balancing innovation, security, governance, cost, and operational feasibility. Strong collaboration skills with the ability to influence across teams and organizational boundaries without direct authority. Working knowledge of responsible technology adoption, AI governance, risk management, access controls, and enterprise control environments. This position requires fluent written and oral communication in English. Applicants must be authorized to work for any employer in the U.S. We are unable to sponsor or take over sponsorship of an employment Visa at this time. Our Culture & Commitment: We’re proud to foster a supportive, inclusive environment where career growth, collaboration, and wellness are prioritized.
