title: Senior Product Marketing Manager
jd_text: We're looking for a Senior Product Marketing Manager to own the positioning strategy for a defined segment of the general contractor market. At Procore, Product Marketing sits inside the product organization as a full peer to Product Management and Design, and Product Marketing is expected to bring market evidence to influence what gets built. To be successful in this role, you bring a point of view before anyone asks for one, your content shows up in live deals, and you can point to a roadmap, positioning, or packaging decision that changed because of your win/loss work. The construction vertical is ripe for technological innovation. Construction impacts the lives of nearly everyone in the world, and yet it's one of the least digitized industries. Procore is leading the market with our SaaS construction platform. We build for real people with real experiences, empowering Groundbreakers to develop and transform the communities we all live in. This position reports into the Director of Product Marketing, General Contractors, and will be based in our Austin, TX office, with remote candidates considered. We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll do Own the business metric for an assigned segment of the general contractor market, and report on it proactively Own the positioning strategy for your market, and measure field adoption, message reception in calls, and win rate against competitors Run the go-to-market side of betas and Tier 1 and Tier 2 launches in your segment, thinking backward from how general contractors will hear and buy the thing while it's still being built Keep a complete, current artifact portfolio for [segment] across the full revenue lifecycle, covering what sellers and SEs need to win new business and what customers, AMs, and CSEs need to retain and expand it Participate in 10+ customer engagements a week with general contractors, and surface market signal that changes at least one roadmap or positioning conversation a quarter Build repeatable AI workflows for your segment across call mining, competitive monitoring, and content generation, and hold the quality bar on everything they produce What we're looking for Bachelor's degree or equivalent experience 4+ years of product marketing or equivalent experience in enterprise SaaS, or comparable experience in the construction industry, with direct experience marketing to general contractors strongly preferred Evidence of owning positioning strategy rather than executing it, including a change you made and the in-market result you measured Fluency handling objections against Autodesk, Trimble ProjectSight, and the point solutions that show up in your segment, and a habit of building competitive knowledge from live deals Repeatable AI workflows you've built and can demonstrate, along with a clear account of how you catch and kill AI-generated errors before they ship Excellent listening and communication skills; product marketing is equally about inquiring as it is advocating Additional Information Base Pay Range: 129,600.00 - 178,200.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. title: Manager, Database Engineering
jd_text: As passionate about our people as we are about our mission. Why Join Q2? Q2 is a leading provider of digital banking and lending solutions to banks, credit unions, alternative finance companies, and fintechs in the U.S. and internationally. Our mission is simple: build strong and diverse communities through innovative financial technology—and we do that by empowering our people to help create success for our customers. What Makes Q2 Special? Being as passionate about our people as we are about our mission. We celebrate our employees in many ways through our year-round Q2 ChangeMakers awards program and global moments of recognition and connection. We invest in the growth and development of our team members through ongoing learning opportunities, internal mobility, and meaningful leadership relationships. We also know that nothing builds trust and collaboration like having fun and giving back together. From company-wide volunteer days to events like our Q2 Homecoming Week—featuring learning, community service, and culture-building experiences—we create opportunities to connect, grow, and make an impact. Summary We run a large SQL Server estate at serious scale, mostly on EC2, alongside a fast-growing set of PostgreSQL, Aurora, Snowflake, MongoDB, and Pinecone workloads supporting analytical and AI use cases. We are primarily an AWS shop with a small Azure footprint, and this team keeps that estate fast, available, recoverable, and cost-efficient for the financial institutions that depend on it. We are looking for a manager who owns production and drives our engineers to be the best versions of themselves. Not someone who reacts to what breaks, but someone who anticipates risk, guides a highly skilled team to the best solution, and drives programs end to end without being told to. Patching and maintenance are an afterthought for us; the successful candidate is already thinking about the problems the team hasn't realized it has yet. A defining trait of this team is that we build our own solutions rather than outsource: we build custom tooling so we can scale with technology instead of people, while knowing the line where a vendor solves it more economically. We serve two sets of customers who both matter deeply. Externally, a bad day for us can mean a bank that anchors a local community is unavailable to the people who depend on it. Internally, our stakeholders are other Q2'ers, and the goal is to multiply their impact through self-service tooling to the point where they don't need a DBA at all. Responsibilities Own production: accountable for availability, performance, and recoverability across the multi-engine estate. Own the coverage model and act as the incident-command backstop so the team, not any one person, carries a bad day Set technical direction and own the outcome. Guide highly skilled engineers to the best solution, mentoring rather than driving where that serves better, and tell senior stakeholders where we are going and why Champion build-our-own tooling and self-service, with the judgment to know where a vendor is the more economical answer Push AI hands-on to build observability into the stack and extend the tooling we have already built Grow the team and hold it accountable to the value it delivers: coach, set clear expectations, and run honest performance conversations Own the economics: enterprise licensing and annual true-up, storage right-sizing, and cost-to-serve. Track spend and defend the numbers to finance and leadership Set the standards for availability-group and DR design, build and automation practices, and data security and access control aligned with governance policy Lead modernization end to end: version migrations, cross-engine consolidation, and DR maturation, driven to measurable milestones Establish engineering rhythms, KPIs, and accountability, and partner across data platform, architecture, and product to deliver curated data products Experience and Knowledge Typically requires a Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field and a minimum of 6 years of related experience; or an advanced degree with 4+ years of experience Typically requires 1-2 years managing and developing employees Deep SQL Server expertise at scale: Always On availability groups, multi-region high availability and DR, performance troubleshooting, and enterprise licensing economics Ability to lead engineers across multiple database technologies: relational (SQL Server, PostgreSQL, Aurora), analytical (Snowflake), and non-relational or specialized stores (MongoDB, vector databases such as Pinecone). Expertise in all is not required, but you must guide direction, judge quality, and grow specialists across the estate Strong AWS depth running a database estate primarily on EC2, treating cloud cost as a first-class engineering concern; working Azure knowledge is useful A track record of defining and driving programs end to end, including migration or modernization work you initiated and owned, not just projects you were assigned Robust, hands-on AI ability to build observability and tooling quickly; this is critical, not optional Strong judgment under pressure and a bias to own the ambiguous, unowned problem rather than route it away Familiarity with security, compliance, and operational best practices; financial services or other regulated, high-availability experience preferred This position requires fluent written and oral communication in English. title: QA Engineer 2 - DroneDeploy
jd_text: DroneDeploy, the robotics and visual intelligence platform for the built world that is used on over 3 million jobsites across more than 180 countries, is now a part of Procore Technologies Inc., the global provider of construction management software. As a leader in reality capture and robotic automation, DroneDeploy delivers the visual intelligence that bridges the built world—from active construction sites to operational assets—and the digital world, providing critical, real-time visibility into daily operations. Procore Technologies is the leading technology partner for every stage of construction. We empower construction teams to drive efficiency and mitigate risk through actionable AI & data-driven insights. For over 20 years, we have been transforming the industry with purpose-built solutions for construction professionals and we’re looking for talented people to help us build together. We are looking for a Quality Assurance (QA) Engineer 2 to elevate quality across our core web experience. As the Quality Assurance (QA) Engineer on our Core Web Product Team, you will work closely with Engineering, Product, and Design to ensure product reliability, strengthen customer workflows, and enable confident software delivery. Your strengths in risk-based test strategy, Playwright/TypeScript automation, and AI-accelerated test design will drive your success. You will report to the Lead QA Engineer and will be a 2 day per week hybrid role located in the Austin Texas office. This position will require 1–2 trips per quarter to customer sites. Partner directly with customers during field and site visits to validate real-world workflows and bring user context into exploratory testing decisions. Plan and execute functional, exploratory, regression, and release testing while maintaining accurate test management records. Create and maintain web, API, and end-to-end automation using TypeScript and Playwright to improve release confidence and accelerate feedback. Investigate failures independently, reproduce defects, analyze root causes, and author clear bug reports to speed up resolution. Collaborate across functions to surface risks, address recurring quality gaps, and optimize team-wide testing workflows. Integrate AI tooling into daily QA workflows to accelerate test design, regression maintenance, bug prioritization, and metrics analysis. What You Bring Demonstrated experience in QA or Quality Engineering with a focus on web-based products and complex workflows. Hands-on automation experience using TypeScript, Playwright, or comparable web/API automation frameworks. Proven capability in designing risk-based, customer-centered testing strategies and conducting independent failure investigations (using browser tools, logs, and APIs). Experience integrating and troubleshooting automated tests in CI/CD pipelines, including test selection, environment setup, and reporting. Practical experience using AI tools to assist in test design, automation creation, or defect analysis. Strong communication skills for documenting defects, detailing test coverage, and conveying release risks clearly. Familiarity with geospatial, mapping, 3D, or media-rich data products, or testing under load/performance constraints is a plus. Behind our customers - amazing companies that help feed the world, provide life-saving medicine on a global scale, and focus on clean water and green mobility - our people are energized problem solvers that take pride in how the work we do changes the world for the better. We welcome all makers, forward thinkers, and problem solvers who are looking for a place to do their best work. And if that’s you we would love to have you join us! Job Description Are you a proactive problem-solver who thrives in a fast-paced environment? Join Rockwell Automation as a trusted partner to senior sales leadership and play a key role in keeping our Houston office running seamlessly. In this highly visible position, you'll combine executive-level administrative support with office operations leadership, helping drive productivity, collaboration, and an exceptional employee and customer experience. If you excel at managing competing priorities, building strong relationships, and staying one step ahead, this is an opportunity to make a meaningful impact. We are looking for a balance of executive-level administrative expertise, operational rigor, and proactive sales support, with a focus on administration, office operations, efficiency, responsiveness, and partnership. This work may be highly confidential in nature and requires attention to detail, proactive action, management of multiple priorities and implementation with minimal direction. As the primary point of contact for the assigned location, the incumbent requires strong collaboration. This is a hybrid role based in our Houston office, and reports into the Vice President of Global Market Access. Your Responsibilities: Provide high-level administrative support to senior sales leaders, including calendar management, travel coordination, and meeting planning. Manage complex schedules, priorities, and confidential communications across multiple stakeholders and time zones. Coordinate domestic and international travel, expenses, budgets, purchase orders, and expense reconciliation. Serve as the primary point of contact for office operations, facilities, vendors, and employee support. Support onboarding activities, including workspace setup, technology access, and coordination with IT and HR. Organize regional sales meetings, customer events, training sessions, and executive visits. Track key business initiatives, action items, and deadlines to support leadership teams. Partner with Sales, HR, Finance, IT, Marketing, and other functions to ensure smooth business operations. Help with hiring activities, including interview scheduling and candidate experience coordination. Identify opportunities to improve processes, increase efficiency, and maintain compliance with company policies. Maintain accurate records, documentation, and audit-ready files. Build strong relationships across the organization while providing professional, customer-focused support. Demonstrate excellent communication, discretion, adaptability, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. The Essentials - You Will Have: High School Diploma or equivalent. Legal authorization to work in the US is required. We will not sponsor individuals for employment visas, now or in the future, for this role. The Preferred - You Might Also Have: Minimum of four years of related experience. Must have excellent communication and organizational skills. Prior administrative, office, executive or other related sales support Human Resources related courses or a two year degree. We require advanced use of Windows and Microsoft Office Proficiency in the use of Microsoft SharePoint. The ability to compose a customer-quality PowerPoint presentation. What We Offer: Health Insurance including Medical, Dental and Vision 401k Paid Time off Parental and Caregiver Leave Flexible Work Schedule where you will work with your manager to enjoy a work schedule that can be flexible with your personal life. To learn more about our benefits package, please visit at www.raquickfind.com . At Rockwell Automation we are dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive and authentic workplace, so if you're excited about this role but your experience doesn't align perfectly with every qualification in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this or other roles. #LI-Hybrid #LI-LH2 This position is part of a job family. Experience will be the determining factor for position level and compensation. We are an Equal Opportunity Employer including disability and veterans. If you are an individual with a disability and you need assistance or a reasonable accommodation during the application process, please contact our services team at +1 (844) 404-7247. Rockwell Automation’s hybrid policy aligns that employees are expected to work at a Rockwell location at least Mondays, Tuesdays, and Thursdays unless they have a business obligation out of the office.

title: Principal Site Reliability Engineer, AI Automation and Orchestration
jd_text: We’re looking for a Principal Site Reliability Engineer to join Procore’s Compute Division to work on our FedRAMP initiative. In this role, you’ll help build Procore’s next-generation construction compute platform for others to build upon, including Procore developers, analysts, partners, and customers. As a Principal Site Reliability Engineer , you’ll partner with other engineers and product managers across Product & Technology to develop and maintain compute platform capabilities that enable SaaS based products to operate in a FedRAMP compliant environment. To be successful in this role, you’re passionate about distributed systems on the cloud with experience in operating and maintaining cloud based products at-scale. If you’re an engineer comfortable and excited about building our next-generation platform and translating problems into pragmatic solutions that open up the boundaries of technical possibilities—we’d love to hear from you! This position reports to the Director of Infrastructure Platform and and is a hybrid role based out of our Austin, TX office . We’re looking for someone to join us immediately. This position requires US citizenship to work on FedRAMP-compliant projects. Candidates must be eligible to work on federal government projects requiring FedRAMP authorization. title: Critical Operations Technician I
jd_text: Who we are: As a global leader in digital infrastructure, QTS designs, builds and operates advanced data centers that support strategic AI, cloud and digital transformation initiatives. We are driven by a mission to connect the world for good and our people make it possible. Every single day, the creativity, dedication and genuine care for our communities are what push us forward and make this a truly special place to be. SUMMARY The Critical Operations Technician I is responsible for the installation, repair, and maintenance of IT, electrical, mechanical, plumbing/piping equipment, machinery and controls located in the interior and exterior of building. This role monitors operations and conducts a routine and ongoing assessment of the building systems, operations, and performance. This role performs tests, rounds and analyzes data to ensure the proper functioning of departmental equipment. The role is also responsible for assisting customers on the Data Center floor both in person and via the telephone, performing customer equipment installs, managing tickets within the ticketing system, communicating and escalating alerts and customer requests to systems engineers for resolution, and completing tasks pertaining to computer hardware, software or operation systems. This role requires on-site work hours to support a 24X7X365 data center environment and is not eligible for remote and/or hybrid work. RESPONSIBILITIES, other duties may be assigned. Applies learning, knowledge, skills, and company policies to a wide range of tasks pertaining to IT, electrical and mechanical equipment, controls, and operating systems. Leads, maintains, monitors, and performs preventive maintenance on mechanical and electrical equipment; records readings and adjusts where necessary to ensure proper operation of equipment. Provide remote hands and eyes services for customers. Provide high level computer hardware and software configuration support. Install suite wall, cage material, ladder rack, fiber tray, cabinets, cabling, and customer equipment based on documentation provided by provisioning documentation and established Data Center Operation procedures. Installs and repairs IT, mechanical, and electrical equipment as required; assists other team members with major repairs and maintenance of building and equipment. Process work orders for preventative and corrective maintenance on critical, building, and site infrastructure. Consults with supervisor or team lead to order necessary tools and equipment as required to complete all maintenance and perform necessary work. Create and/or update tickets within the established ticketing system to address customer calls, data center facility, network and/or system related alerts. Operates and monitors critical and non-critical system equipment and components to ensure safe and compliant operation. Responds as required to building emergencies and customer requests. Complies with departmental policy for the safe storage, usage, and disposal of hazardous materials. Uses the Change Management Process to get approval for preventative and corrective maintenance. title: Principal Product Manager, Compliance and Payments (New Markets)
jd_text: We're looking for a Principal Product Manager to join Procore's Product & Technology organization, supporting our Procore Pay business . In this role, you'll identify, size, and validate the next set of markets and segments for Procore's Compliance and Payments products, turning early signals into fully formed strategies backed by evidence. Your primary goal is to determine where Procore Pay can win next — and to prove product-market fit in those markets before we scale investment behind them. As a Principal Product Manager , you'll partner with Engineering, UX, Product Marketing, Sales, Finance, Risk & Compliance, and Payments leadership to move opportunities from a hypothesis to a funded, launched, revenue-generating product line. Use your opportunity assessment and market sizing rigor, customer discovery expertise, and ability to operate independently in ambiguity to expand the Procore Pay product and open new revenue streams for Procore. This is a rare chance to shape a strategically critical, high-growth part of Procore's business with real autonomy and executive visibility — apply today. This position reports into the Director of Product Management, Procore Pay and will be based in our Austin, TX office . We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll do: Lead opportunity assessments for new markets and segments, sizing the opportunity and making a clear, defensible recommendation on whether and how Procore should enter. Validate product-market fit for existing Procore Pay capabilities in new markets, defining the discovery plan, entry criteria, and evidence required before we commit resources. Craft the vision, opportunity assessments, and product briefs for your area, explaining the "why" with sound logic that holds up to executive scrutiny. Take large, ambiguous strategic initiatives and break them into logical, sequenced phases that deliver value to customers along the way. Lead discovery with customers, prospects, and industry participants, facilitating workshops with department leaders and directors and synthesizing findings into actionable insights. Partner with Engineering and UX as a peer leader to translate market strategy into requirements, anticipating risk factors across outcome potential, competitive landscape, technical feasibility, and user experience. Drive go-to-market readiness with Marketing, Sales, Enablement, Support, Risk, and Compliance, designing release plans that generate fast learning through pilots and betas. Define initiative-level customer and business outcomes, track progress against them, and communicate results in a compelling way across Procore. Mentor product managers and contribute to hiring panels, raising the bar for product craft across the team. What we're looking for: 7+ years of product management or equivalent experience, including ownership of a large or strategically important product area. Demonstrated track record of new market or new product entry: taking a small, unproven idea and developing it into a funded, launched, revenue-generating initiative. Expertise in opportunity assessment, market sizing, and product-market fit validation, with the judgment to recommend against an opportunity when the evidence doesn't support it. Expert command of discovery techniques through customer interviews, market and competitive analysis, prototype testing, and the ability to synthesize findings into trends others can act on. Strong quantitative skills, with the ability to pull and analyze data independently and combine it with qualitative insight to make high-leverage decisions quickly. Proven ability to work autonomously amid significant ambiguity, serving as the connective tissue when ownership is unclear and biasing toward forward progress. Excellent written and verbal communication, with a history of building buy-in among senior stakeholders across multiple functions without formal authority. Construction Compliance, Payments, fintech, or B2B marketplace experience strongly preferred; construction industry experience is a plus. title: Senior Organic Analytics Manager
jd_text: Risepoint is an education technology company that helps regional universities launch and grow online programs for modern learners. Risepoint supports more than 100 universities and colleges across five countries, with programs concentrated in high-demand fields including nursing, healthcare, teaching, business, technology, and public service. Our suite of products and services supports the full student journey and each university’s long-term goals. Together, we increase access to affordable education that delivers a strong return on investment for learners and meets employer and community needs. Learn more at risepoint.com. The Impact You Will Make This role helps Risepoint understand how organic discovery, AI search, and the digital experience contribute to student demand and enrollment. The Senior Manager, Organic Analytics will lead day-to-day analytical work across SEO, answer engine optimization (AEO), website/DXP performance, and the organic funnel. By connecting visibility and website behavior to leads, applications, and enrollments, this person will help the organization understand what happened, why it happened, where it is concentrated, and what actions should follow. How You Will Bring Our Mission to Life The Senior Manager, Organic Analytics is the primary day-to-day analytics partner for SEO, AEO, organic content, and DXP/CRO measurement within Channel Analytics. Working under the direction of the Sr. Director, Channel Analytics, this person leads analytical execution, develops measurement approaches, defines business and reporting requirements, conducts deep-dive analyses, and translates findings into clear recommendations. They partner closely with Analytics Solutions, which develops production dashboards, as well as SEO/AEO, Digital Experience, CRO, CRM, Data Engineering, and other analytics stakeholders. The role measures and evaluates organic strategy; it does not own SEO/content execution. What You Will Do • Lead monthly Organic MBR analysis and recurring performance diagnosis across SEO, AEO, website/DXP, and the organic funnel, including traffic, leads, applications/enrollments where available, conversion, YoY/MoM drivers, where performance is concentrated, opportunities, and risks. • Analyze SEO performance using GA4, Google Search Console, and SEO platforms, including impressions, clicks, CTR, rankings/visibility, branded vs. non-branded demand where useful, landing-page/content performance, and where performance gains or declines are concentrated. • Lead AEO measurement across AI visibility, citations, Citation Share/Share of Voice, prompts/topics, engine-level performance, AI referral traffic, competitive/source analysis, and downstream outcomes; partner with Profound or similar platform data as available. • Design measurement for AEO, SEO, DXP, and CRO initiatives by establishing baselines, intervention dates, comparison groups or matched controls where appropriate, and post-launch reads; evaluate uncertainty, confounding, and whether observed changes are reasonably attributable to the intervention. • Measure website and funnel performance from organic/AI discovery through landing-page behavior, forms, leads, applications, and enrollments; distinguish traffic-driven changes from conversion-driven changes and evaluate DXP migrations, site releases, and CRO changes. • Reconcile GA4/GSC/SEO/AEO/CRM data, investigate material Organic performance changes, identify tracking or taxonomy issues before results reach leadership, and translate findings into 2–4 decision-ready insights rather than metric dumps. • Define KPI logic, reporting requirements, analytical views, intervention/change logs, and data-quality needs; partner with Antonio/Analytics Solutions and Data Engineering to bring GA4, GSC, AEO platform, Salesforce, and intervention data into scalable reporting and Databricks-based workflows rather than relying on manual Excel processes. What Success Looks Like • Organic MBR analysis is delivered with clear drivers, concentrations, business implications, and recommended actions, allowing the Sr. Director to review and sharpen the story rather than perform the first-pass analysis. • SEO, AEO, and DXP performance can be connected from visibility and search demand through website behavior, leads, applications, and enrollments, with known data limitations clearly documented. • AEO reporting moves from manual snapshots toward a scalable history and measurement process with clear hero metrics, engine-level views, prompt/topic and URL-level analysis, intervention tracking, and credible post-launch reads. • Material Organic, content, and website changes can be diagnosed quickly, including whether movement reflects demand, visibility, traffic quality, conversion, tracking, taxonomy, or maturation effects. • The Senior Manager becomes the primary day-to-day analytics partner for Organic, AEO, and Digital Experience stakeholders, increasing Channel Analytics capacity while the Sr. Director retains overall strategy, prioritization, and cross-channel accountability. How Impact Will be Measured • Reliability, adoption, and usefulness of Organic MBR analysis and recurring SEO, AEO, DXP/CRO, and funnel reporting. • Quality of business requirements, KPI definitions, analytical specifications, and data QA provided to Analytics Solutions and Data Engineering. • Improved visibility into organic traffic quality, search/content effectiveness, AI-search performance, website conversion, and progression through application and enrollment. • Quality and credibility of pilot, test, migration, and rollout measurement, including appropriate treatment of baselines, comparison groups, intervention timing, uncertainty, and confounding. • Clarity and actionability of recommendations and evidence that insights influence SEO/AEO, content, DXP/CRO, partner, and prioritization decisions. • Reduction in repetitive manual analysis and stakeholder confidence in the Organic analytics story presented to leadership. What You’ll Bring to the Team Experience & Skills That Matter Most (Required) • 6+ years of hands-on experience in digital/web analytics, organic/SEO analytics, marketing analytics, or a closely related data-driven environment, with demonstrated strength diagnosing performance rather than only producing reports. • Advanced SQL skills and the ability to independently pull, join, QA, and investigate complex web, marketing, and CRM datasets in cloud data environments. • Strong analytical proficiency with GA4 and Google Search Console plus working knowledge of SEO data/tools such as Ahrefs, Semrush, or equivalent; understand traffic sources, landing pages, events, funnels, rankings/visibility, queries, content performance, and technical SEO concepts. • Strong funnel analytics skills, including the ability to connect sessions and website behavior to leads, applications, enrollments, conversion rates, cohort/maturation considerations, and known attribution or identity-resolution limitations. • Strong analytical diagnosis, data QA, and executive storytelling skills: identify whether unusual results are real or caused by tracking/taxonomy issues and translate findings into what happened, why, where it is concentrated, and what should happen next. • Experience defining KPI logic, business requirements, and reporting specifications for BI/Analytics Solutions teams; strong Excel skills and enough data-visualization fluency to design useful reporting without being the production dashboard developer. • Working knowledge of experimentation and causal measurement concepts, including pre/post design, control or matched-comparison groups, confounding, uncertainty/statistical significance, and the limits of correlation; deep experimental-design expertise is not required. Experience That’s Great to Have (Preferred) • AEO/generative-search literacy, including citations vs. mentions, prompts and prompt themes, AI visibility/Share of Voice, source attribution, branded vs. non-branded prompts, engine differences, AI referrals, zero-click/offsite discovery, and experience with Profound, Ahrefs Brand Radar, Semrush AI visibility tools, or similar platforms. • Deeper experimentation/causal-inference experience, including matched controls, difference-in-differences, natural experiments, incrementality, or rollout measurement; Python or R experience for large-scale prompt/citation analysis, URL classification, topic clustering, or competitor analysis is also valuable. • Experience with Databricks, BigQuery, Snowflake, Salesforce data, Power BI, GSC/API data, web scraping/log-file analysis, DXP/CRO teams, or higher-education/high-consideration lead-generation environments. Risepoint is an equal-opportunity employer and supports a diverse and inclusive workforce.

title: Principal Product Manager, Developer Platform
jd_text: We're looking for a Principal Product Manager who thinks like an engineer, advocates for developers, and builds like a founder — to reshape Procore's development platform for the AI era.. In this role you'll shape the future of Procore's development platform by treating our 1,000+ internal developers as your customers, and the developer platform as your product. You'll own the developer platform roadmap. You'll know our developers better than anyone — what they're building, where they stall, what they've stopped bothering to ask for — and you'll turn that into a point of view sharp enough to change what gets built across Procore. And you'll build it for a second customer almost nobody has designed for yet: the thousands of agents those developers are running. Human in the loop, not human in the driver's seat. That's what makes this rare. Most platform PMs are optimizing a portal. You'll be designing the interface between an engineering organization and its agents — at the exact moment that interface is being invented. Get it right and 1,000 engineers feel it every single day. This position reports a Group Product Manager and will be based in our Austin, TX office. We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll own The golden paths. You define them, and you make them so good that going around them stops being tempting. Build, test, and deploy that feels the same whether it's Ruby or Go. Preview environments that just work. Pipelines nobody wants to escape. Infrastructure that answers in minutes. Developers declare what they need; the platform resolves it inside a policy envelope — the right shape, the right region, costed and approved before it exists. You'll turn provisioning into a capability engineers call instead of a request they file. Security and compliance as guardrails, not gates. Experience making security, compliance, or cost a property of the platform rather than a tax on teams — policy as code, automated remediation, spend attributed to the team that spent it. Observability and cost, built in by default. Every service born instrumented and attributed — dashboards and alerts live from day one, spend visible to the team that owns it, and telemetry an agent can reason over whether the question is a 2 a.m. incident or an unexplained jump in spend. The agent-native platform. Typed, discoverable capabilities that people and agents call the same way, through the same gates and the same audit trail. Agents do the toil and bring the proof; humans keep the judgment. Very few product managers get to design this layer right now — you'd be one of them. The opinion. You set the point of view. This is an organization ready for someone to say "this is how we build here" and then back it up with something engineers genuinely want to use. What we're looking for 8+ years building infrastructure, platform, or developer tools at SaaS scale — with at least one platform you can point at and say "I built that, here's who used it and why." You've been an engineer, architect, SRE, or in DevRel. Close enough to the work that you could do it yourself. Hands-on depth across the modern stack — Kubernetes, IaC, CI/CD, GitOps, secrets — and opinions about which layers deserve abstraction and which deserve exposure. Real observability chops as part of that breadth: OpenTelemetry, distributed tracing, metrics and logging pipelines, and the aggregators around them. A track record of being opinionated in public — and the receipts. A path you chose, the people who pushed back, and what adoption looked like a year later. Plugged in outside your own walls — CNCF, platform-engineering communities, the rooms where this is actually being figured out. A working view of how agentic development changes what a platform has to guarantee. Not "we should add AI." The temperament to sit with a skeptical senior engineer, understand their architecture, and co-create the fix. Repeatedly. title: Staff Engineer, AI Automation and Orchestration
jd_text: Procore Technologies is building the software that builds the world. We provide cloud-based construction management software that helps clients more efficiently build skyscrapers, hospitals, retail centers, airports, housing complexes, and more. At Procore, we have worked hard to create and maintain a culture where you can own your work and are encouraged and given resources to try new ideas. We are looking for a Staff Engineer, AI Automation and Orchestration to join Procore's Government Engineering team and serve as a senior technical contributor for our FedRAMP initiative. In this role, you will design, build, and maintain next-generation platform services that provide cloud traffic, ingress/egress, identity, and compliance capabilities. You will combine your technical and collaboration skills along with established software design principles to create a secure, compliant, and highly scalable foundation that Procore developers, partners, and customers can easily integrate with. The impact of this team is wide as it touches all aspects of Procore's ecosystem within our FedRAMP authorization boundaries, and MUST respect and protect those boundaries. This position reports to the Senior Engineering Manager of the Government Engineering team and is a hybrid role based out of our Austin, TX office. This position requires US citizenship to work on FedRAMP-compliant projects. Candidates must be eligible to work on federal government projects requiring FedRAMP authorization. What you’ll do: Manage Cloud Traffic & Service Mesh technologies: Design, implement, and maintain our next-generation network routing, edge controls, and service mesh architecture using Istio, Kong, and Cloudflare . Lead Platform Migrations: Drive the engineering lifecycle and migration strategies transitioning internal teams over to centralized, compliant infrastructure pipelines using Istio, and Datadog . Manage Identity & Access: Design and implement robust Identity and Access Management (IAM) architectures within FedRAMP boundaries, leveraging Okta for identity federation (SAML/OIDC), SSO, RBAC, and zero-trust patterns. Enforce Cryptographic Security: Select, configure, and enforce NIST-certified FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated cryptographic modules across services, TLS configurations, and key management systems. Advise on FedRAMP Compliance: Serve as a technical subject matter expert on FedRAMP compliance controls (NIST SP 800-53), translating complex regulatory control language into concrete, automated technical implementations. Partner with security teams on continuous monitoring (ConMon) and annual assessment readiness. Develop Automations: Actively write production-grade software to eliminate platform gaps while mentoring mid-level engineers on compliance-aware engineering design patterns. Leverage AI Tools: Welcome the use of modern developer tooling—including AI-assisted development assistants—where appropriate to optimize coding efficiency, automate mundane tasks, and accelerate platform delivery. What we’re looking for: Experience: 8+ years of software or infrastructure engineering experience, with at least 3 years directly supporting or operating within a FedRAMP-authorized environment (AWS GovCloud experience is a plus). Software Engineering Proficiency: Strong programming fundamentals with demonstrated proficiency in writing software (e.g., Golang, Typescript, or Python) to build robust platform infrastructure and automation tools. Deep IAM Expertise: Comprehensive hands-on experience with identity management architecture, identity federation (SAML, OIDC), directory services, privileged access management, and zero-trust architecture principles. FIPS Cryptography Real-World Experience: Deep understanding of FIPS 140-2/140-3 validated cryptographic modules. You know how to verify and enforce true NIST-certified algorithm/module testing in practice, rather than just knowing "encryption is on." Cloud Traffic & Edge Infrastructure: Production experience managing high-throughput ingress/egress, traffic routing, and container network interfaces at scale using tools like Istio, Kong, and Cloudflare. Kubernetes Ecosystem Mastery: Extensive experience architecting, operating, and hardening Kubernetes clusters, including policy enforcement (e.g., OPA/Gatekeeper, Kyverno) and secure secrets management., Experience with secrets management platforms operating in FIPS mode (e.g., HashiCorp Vault). Familiarity with FedRAMP Rev 5 transition requirements. Experience with STIG application or CIS benchmark enforcement at scale. Security certifications such as CISSP, AWS Certified Security - Specialty, or CKS. jd_text: DroneDeploy, the robotics and visual intelligence platform for the built world that is used on over 3 million jobsites across more than 180 countries, is now a part of Procore Technologies Inc., the global provider of construction management software. As a leader in reality capture and robotic automation, DroneDeploy delivers the visual intelligence that bridges the built world—from active construction sites to operational assets—and the digital world, providing critical, real-time visibility into daily operations. Procore Technologies is the leading technology partner for every stage of construction. We empower construction teams to drive efficiency and mitigate risk through actionable AI & data-driven insights. For over 20 years, we have been transforming the industry with purpose-built solutions for construction professionals and we’re looking for talented people to help us build together. We are looking for a Customer Success Manager to manage a high-volume portfolio (~70+ mid-market AEC accounts) and drive customer health, adoption, retention, and revenue expansion. As the CSM, AEC Mid-Market on our AEC Customer Success team, you will work closely with Sales, Solutions, Services, Product Support, and Product Management to align our reality capture platform to customer outcomes. Your strengths in portfolio management, consultative engagement, and cross-functional collaboration will drive your success. You will report to the Manager, Customer Success and will be based in Austin, Texas, aligning to U.S. Central/Eastern core collaboration hours with ~15–20% domestic travel. What You’ll Do Manage a portfolio of ~70+ mid-market AEC customers, with clear ownership for health, adoption, retention, and growth to maximize time-to-value. Build and execute account plans that achieve portfolio-level revenue growth (target ~20% YoY) and strong net/gross retention. Lead onboarding and early lifecycle motions to establish core workflows, effective training, and rapid platform realization. Monitor usage and health signals to intervene early, addressing adoption gaps, risks, and new opportunities proactively. Co-own renewals with Sales by forecasting, preparing, and running reviews to drive timely execution of contracts. Identify and qualify expansion opportunities (license growth, new units, add-ons) and partner with Sales to secure them. Act as a trusted advisor on reality capture workflows and program design for AEC customers. Represent the voice of the customer to Product, Support, and Services, providing structured feedback and use-case insight. Coordinate with Support and Services to resolve issues quickly and maintain confidence in the platform. Utilize Salesforce, Gong, and Glean to prepare for meetings, capture insights, and maintain clear documentation. What You Bring 3+ years in B2B Customer Success, Account Management, or a similar customer-facing SaaS role to bring proven experience in driving retention and growth. Proven track record of managing and growing a defined book of business across a sizeable portfolio of accounts with structured planning. Strong consultative, data-driven approach to customer engagement, value realization, and business outcome alignment. Excellent written and verbal communication skills across field users, operations, and executive leadership. High CRM discipline and a strong habit of clear, timely documentation using tools like Salesforce, Gong, and collaboration platforms. Ability to obtain a USA Part 107 Drone License within the first 90–120 days of employment and maintain it throughout employment. Ability and willingness to travel domestically ~15–20% for customer visits and company events. Strong-fit Background Might Include B2B SaaS Customer Success Management / Account Management AEC (Architecture, Engineering, Construction) Industry Operations or Technology Drone / Reality Capture Program Management Construction Field Management or Jobsite Technology Specialist Additional Information Base Pay Range: 105,600.00 - 145,200.00 USD Annual On Target Earning Range: 132,000.00 - 181,500.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Actual compensation will be based on a candidate’s job-related skills, experience, education or training, and location. title: Infra Electrical Operations & Maintenance Manager
jd_text: About Samsung Austin Semiconductor Samsung is a world leader in advanced semiconductor technology, founded on the belief that the pursuit of excellence creates a better world. At Samsung Austin Semiconductor, we are Innovating Today to Power the Devices of Tomorrow. Come innovate with us! Position Summary The Infrastructure Electrical Operations and Maintenance (O&M) Manager is responsible for ensuring the reliability, availability, and maintenance of all electrical power distribution systems. This position is critical for maintaining the continuous, safe, and efficient operation of the electrical infrastructure necessary to support round-the-clock manufacturing operations. The role requires extensive experience in managing complex electrical O&M (Operations & Maintenance) programs, including preventative maintenance (PM), predictive maintenance (PdM), and emergency corrective actions in a high-stakes industrial environment. The individual in this position is expected to lead the development and optimization of Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) and maintenance workflows to maximize system uptime and eliminate single points of failure. Operational excellence must be achieved with an absolute emphasis on safety, incident reduction, and rigorous adherence to electrical codes. Samsung Austin Semiconductor is a 24/7/365 factory where utility interruptions are catastrophic; therefore, a "zero-outage" mindset is mandatory. Role and Responsibilities Here’s What You’ll Be Responsible For: Lead the development, ownership, and auditing of the operational processes and maintenance schedules required to ensure the safe and error-free operation of the electrical grid. Mentor junior operations engineers and technicians in reliability-centered maintenance (RCM) and best practices. Interface with Manufacturing and Equipment teams to manage power load requirements and coordinate planned maintenance windows. Exercise **Extreme Ownership** over the electrical infrastructure, accepting full responsibility for system stability, equipment health, and the rapid restoration of power in the event of a failure. Develop and oversee detailed Method Statements and Risk Assessments for all operational switching, maintenance activities, and emergency repairs to ensure zero safety incidents. Manage third-party maintenance vendors, service contracts, and specialized technicians to ensure all facility electrical assets are maintained to OEM specifications. Lead the Root Cause Analysis (RCA) process for any electrical anomalies or outages, implementing permanent corrective actions to prevent recurrence. Proactively identify aging infrastructure and develop lifecycle replacement plans (CapEx) to mitigate the risk of equipment failure. Perform regular site audits and thermographic/power quality inspections to verify the health of electrical equipment and ensure compliance with safety and NEC standards. Demonstrate strong leadership skills to coordinate between Facilities, Manufacturing, and EHS organizations to balance the need for critical maintenance with the demands of aggressive production schedules. Skills and Qualifications Here's what you'll need: Education, Training, Certification(s) and Minimum years of experience required 4-year degree in Electrical or Electronics Engineering from an ABET accredited institution. Minimum 11 years of experience in electrical operations and maintenance within a heavy industrial setting. Semiconductor fab or Data Center experience is highly preferred. Certified Maintenance & Reliability Professional (CMRP) or PMP certification is a plus. OSHA 30-Hour Construction/General Industry certification is a plus. Knowledge, Skills, Abilities, Software, and Tools Expert knowledge of industrial power distribution systems (Hight/Medium/Low Voltage), switchgear, UPS systems, generators, and ATS, as well as deep familiarity with NEC, NFPA 70E (Electrical Safety in the Workplace). Strong crisis management skills and the ability to lead technical teams under pressure during emergency outage scenarios. Advanced data analysis skills using Microsoft Excel (Pivot Tables, VLOOKUP, Power Query) to track Mean Time Between Failures (MTBF) and Mean Time to Repair (MTTR). Experience with CMMS (Computerized Maintenance Management Systems for tracking work orders, asset history, and PM scheduling. Proficiency with electrical monitoring tools (Power Quality Analyzers, Infrared Thermography, and Arc Flash Analysis software like ETAP or SKM). Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to translate complex technical failures into executive-level briefings. Permanent right to work in US and ability to be "on-call" and work overtime/non-scheduled days to support critical facility emergencies. title: Project Manager Lead, Tool Hookup Electrical
jd_text: About Samsung Austin Semiconductor Samsung is a world leader in advanced semiconductor technology, founded on the belief that the pursuit of excellence creates a better world. At Samsung Austin Semiconductor, we are Innovating Today to Power the Devices of Tomorrow. Come innovate with us! Position Summary The Project Manager (Tool Hookup Electrical) Lead is responsible for overseeing the electrical Tool Hookup Project Managers, providing mentorship and coaching in daily engineering activities, scheduling, and tactical construction execution related to electrical power distribution, instrumentation, and control hookups within a semiconductor foundry. This role operates on the production floor and sub-fab, coordinating directly with trade contractors, field engineers, and equipment vendors to ensure that individual manufacturing tools are connected safely, on schedule, and in strict compliance with technical designs. The position carries direct responsibility for resolving field issues, enforcing construction quality, and driving the electrical hookup sequence for assigned tool sectors. Role and Responsibilities Here’s What You’ll Be Responsible For: Responsibilities Act as the primary field contact for electrical trade contractors, coordinating daily work packages and resolving immediate constraints on the cleanroom floor. Coordinate tactical handoffs between facility infrastructure teams and tool-specific installation crews to maintain steady progress. Monitor and report daily on schedule milestones, manpower levels, and material installation rates for assigned toolsets. Review contractor-submitted Requests for Information (RFIs) and Field Change Orders (FCOs), validating field conditions before escalating for approval. Walk the field daily to enforce strict construction safety standards, zero-tolerance electrical safety rules, and cleanroom protocol compliance. Core Job Functions Oversee the physical installation and connection of Low-Voltage (LV) power runs from power panels and busways directly to the tool chassis. Supervise the wiring, termination, and point-to-point verification of Emergency Off (EMO) circuits, tool interlocks, and Toxic Gas Monitoring System (TGMS) modules. Utilize 3D models in the field to resolve routing conflicts between electrical conduits, cable trays, and neighboring mechanical or structural systems. Direct and document critical field quality checks, including insulation resistance testing (Megger testing), grounding continuity verification, and proper torque labeling on terminations. Coordinate the lockout/tagout (LOTO) and initial energization sequences for individual tools, ensuring all systems are safe to receive power. Generate, track, and systematically close out electrical punchlist items to achieve final system acceptance and handover. Skills and Qualifications Here's what you'll need: Education, Training, Credentials, and Experience Bachelor’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Construction Management, or a related technical discipline; or equivalent practical experience (e.g., journeyman electrician background with extensive industrial leadership). 4+ years of project management or field engineering experience in large-scale industrial electrical construction. Minimum 2 years of direct experience executing construction or tool install activities within an active semiconductor cleanroom environment. OSHA 30-Hour Construction certification is required; Certified Construction Manager (CCM) or initial CAPM/PMP certification is a plus. Mandatory Knowledge, Skills, and Competencies Solid understanding of industrial electrical installations, including rigid conduit bending, wire pulling, panelboard terminations, and grounding methods. Practical familiarity with the National Electrical Code (NEC/NFPA 70) and fundamental electrical safety practices outlined in NFPA 70E. Practical knowledge of cleanroom protocols (Class 10 to Class 1000) and tools required to prevent contamination during active construction drilling and cutting. Proficiency in navigating and extracting data from digital information modeling viewers (e.g., Autodesk Navisworks) and project management software. title: Engineering Manager – Workload Identity & Secrets Platform
jd_text: Procore runs thousands of services across multiple production regions, and too many of them still authenticate with static, long-lived credentials. We're replacing that model with a Vault-backed identity platform where credentials are short-lived, issued on demand, and tied to workload identity — not to a secret someone pasted into a config file three years ago. We're hiring an Engineering Manager to lead the team that owns that platform. You'll manage a focused team of 4–6 engineers, including senior and staff ICs already deep in this domain, and own the roadmap for how every engineer at Procore gets, rotates, and retires a credential. To be straightforward about the shape of the job: this is a small, senior team, so you'll be partnering closely with your engineers on the ground. Success in this role requires a balance of strong team leadership and technical credibility. You won't be the primary implementer — your staff engineers own the designs and write the code — but rather than managing purely from a distance, you’ll be actively engaged in architectural decisions, making defensible build-vs-buy calls, and building deep system context to help the team navigate tradeoffs and tackle complex, specialized work together. This position reports to a Senior Manager within the Developer Acceleration group and will be based in our Austin,TX office. We're looking for someone to join us immediately. What you'll do: The migration off static credentials. Driving adoption of dynamic, identity-based credentials across Procore's service estate — not just building the platform, but getting teams to move onto it. Developer experience for secrets. Self-service provisioning, credential lifecycle, certificate rotation, and the standards that make the secure path the easy path. The team. Hiring, growing, and retaining engineers across US and international time zones, including career development for senior and staff ICs in a narrow specialty. Reliability of a Tier-0 dependency. When the secrets platform degrades, deploys stop. SLOs, on-call health, and incident response are yours. Partnership with Security Engineering. Aligning platform investment against real compliance and audit obligations without turning your team into a ticket queue. Prioritization under ambiguity. This domain generates far more demand than a six-person team can absorb. Deciding what not to do is a core part of the job. What we're looking for: 2+ years managing software or infrastructure engineering teams, including senior or staff ICs 7+ years total engineering experience, with hands-on background in backend systems, distributed infrastructure, or platform engineering Direct experience with secrets management or identity infrastructure — Vault or equivalent, OIDC, PKI, certificate lifecycle, least-privilege access models Complementary — genuinely not required External Secrets Operator, SPIFFE/SPIRE, or workload identity federation Experience in a regulated or audited environment (SOC 2, ISO 27001, FedRAMP) Vendor evaluation and contract negotiation for infrastructure tooling Working fluency in Kubernetes and infrastructure-as-code (Terraform/HCL, Helm) A track record of building internal platforms other engineers actually adopted, plus the influence to drive migrations across teams you don't control Comfort operating a service other teams depend on: SLOs, incident management, on-call Additional Information Base Pay Range: 168,560.00 - 231,770.00 USD Annual This role may also be eligible for Equity Compensation and/or Bonus Incentive Compensation. Procore is committed to offering competitive, fair, and commensurate compensation. title: Sr. Manager, GTM Cycle Planning and Governance
jd_text: Position Summary Bringing Samsung's go-to-market strategy to life requires seamless coordination across functions — and that coordination is what our team drives. We own the operational cadence that keeps strategy, marketing, retail, finance, and accounts teams aligned and moving in the same direction. From GTM planning cycles and quarterly business reviews to executive governance gates, we ensure the right stakeholders have the right information at the right time — and that risks and dependencies are surfaced early and resolved before they impact execution. We are currently seeking a Senior Manager, GTM Cycle Planning and Governance to lead and manage the operational cadence that drives cross-functional alignment and GTM execution across the organization. This role will own the end-to-end program management framework — including quarterly business reviews, planning cycles, and executive governance gates — and will report directly to the Executive Director of Strategic Product Operations & Governance, working closely with cross-functional teams and account team leadership. title: Manager Content Data Engineering
jd_text: Are you passionate about building trusted data products that power search, analytics, and AI experiences? Do you enjoy leading teams, improving data quality, and transforming complex content into valuable customer-facing solutions? About our Team Intelligize is the leading provider of best-in-class content, exclusive news collections, regulatory insights, and powerful analytical tools for compliance, transactional and financial reporting professionals. Intelligize offers a web-based research platform that ensures law firms, accounting firms, corporations, and other organizations stay compliant with government regulations, build stronger deals and agreements, and deliver value to their shareholders and clients. Headquartered in New York City, Intelligize serves Fortune 500 companies, including Starbucks, IBM, Microsoft, Verizon and Walmart, as well as many of the top global law and accounting firms. About the Role You will lead a team responsible for transforming raw legal and regulatory documents into trusted, structured information that powers Intelligize. Your team will be responsible for our processes to ingest content, extract and normalize metadata from both structured and unstructured documents, maintain canonical representations of key business entities such as companies, and ensure that hundreds of metadata enrichment processes continue to produce accurate, reliable results as source formats evolve. A strong understanding of SQL and relational data structures will be important for guiding how data is modeled, queried, validated, and improved over time. You will establish the quality standards, monitoring, and governance needed to ensure that the metadata our products rely on remains trustworthy over time. This includes partnering closely with Product and Engineering teams to make sure the data foundation supports customer-facing search and AI experiences. Responsibilities Lead offshore and internal teams, including hiring, training, performance management, and employee development. Own execution and reliability for content ingestion, metadata extraction, entity resolution, canonical models, and data quality processes. Establish standards, monitoring, SQL-based validation, escalation paths, and review routines to support search and AI capabilities at scale. Partner with Product and Engineering to define structured data and metadata needs for customer-facing search, benchmarking, analytics, and AI experiences. Communicate technical concepts, tradeoffs, and data quality considerations clearly to engineering, product, and business stakeholders. Establish monitoring, quality metrics, and improvement practices to identify regressions, adapt to source-content changes, and improve metadata accuracy and completeness. Plan and deliver data platform enhancements while balancing new capabilities, technical debt, and maintenance priorities. Drive continuous improvement in data quality, reliability, and operational processes. Requirements Experience leading content engineering, data engineering, information engineering, or similar functions focused on transforming structured and unstructured content into trusted information products. Experience leading and developing teams in a management capacity. Advanced understanding of content ingestion, metadata extraction, entity resolution, data modeling, and information quality. Experience automating metadata extraction, normalization, and enrichment pipelines using appropriate rule-based, machine learning, or LLM-based approaches. Strong understanding of normalized data modeling, canonical entity design, metadata schemas, and provenance. Strong proficiency with relational databases, SQL, and data storage technologies, including investigation, validation, monitoring, and analysis activities. Strong analytical, root-cause analysis, and problem-solving skills with a focus on customer-facing data quality and reliability. Ability to collaborate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders and manage competing priorities. title: Maintenance Shop Lead Tech
jd_text: POSITION SUMMARY: Reporting to a Maintenance Supervisor or Maintenance Manager, the Maintenance Lead Technician provides direction to a group of technicians to ensure that all repairs and maintenance of equipment are performed in compliance with the Company’s safety standards and applicable federal and state regulations. The Maintenance Lead Technician is responsible for all chassis (diesel and non-diesel equipment and trucks) and refuse bodywork, including, but not limited to, hydraulic, electrical, heating and air conditioning system maintenance and repair. In addition, the Lead Technician diagnoses more complicated repair work; provides coaching on diagnostic techniques to subordinate technicians; performs external repair inspections to ensure all repair work is done in a safe manner; and schedules the repair work for his or her work group to ensure that all repair and maintenance work is done in a safe and timely manner, reducing lost productivity within the shop. PRINCIPAL RESPONSIBILITIES: Maintains expert knowledge of, and advanced working proficiency in, the following vehicle components and systems, with the ability to perform complex repair maintenance functions, both on-site and on the road:o Chassis component repair and maintenance; Refuse bodies, including control, hydraulic and electrical systems o Air and hydraulic braking systems; o Engine repair and maintenance;o Suspension, drivetrain and steering systems; and o Heating and air conditioning systems. o Performs line maintenance welding and fabrication. o Provides direction to technicians assigned to his or her work group to ensure that all repair and maintenance work is performed in a safe, efficient and timely manner. May plan and schedule repair work to minimize lost productivity. o Inspects repairs done by a third party vendor to ensure all work has been properly completed in accordance with the Company’s safety procedures and federal and state regulations; follows up when necessary. o Performs repair diagnostics on more complex matters. o Identifies the source of malfunctions using a variety of electronic tools. o Completes applicable Company training programs. o Handles Maintenance Supervisor responsibilities, as needed. o Acts as a mentor to technicians. Performs other job-related duties as assigned or apparent. QUALIFICATIONS: Ability to perform inspections and repairs without supervision in some (not all required) of the following heavy truck, or automotive systems:o Suspensions, Steering, General Engine, Transmissions, Brakes, Electrical, Hydraulics, Drive Train, Diesel Emissions. At least 3 years of experience in a role requiring compliance with OSHA Haz Com, OSHA Lock Out Tag Out, and all OSHA fire protection regulations is a plus but not required. At least 1 year of supervisory or lead technician experience is a plus but not required. ASE Heavy Truck Certifications (T1-T8) is a plus but not required. Class B or higher Commercial Driver’s License is a plus but not required Valid Driver’s License. MINIMUM REQUIREMENTS: At least 3 years of experience as a technician working on heavy-duty trucks. For any concerns relating to Republic Services’ commitment to equal opportunity employment, you may contact the AWARE Line at 1-866-3-AWARE-4. ABOUT THE COMPANY Republic Services, Inc. (NYSE: RSG) is a leader in the environmental services industry. We provide customers with the most complete set of products and services, including recycling, waste, special waste, hazardous waste and field services. Our industry-leading commitments to advance circularity and support decarbonization are helping deliver on our vision to partner with customers to create a more sustainable world. In 2025, Republic’s total company revenue was $16.6 billion, and adjusted EBITDA was $5.3 billion. We serve 13 million customers and operate more than 1,000 locations, including collection and transfer stations, recycling and polymer centers, treatment facilities, and landfills. Although we operate across North America, the collection, recycling, treatment, or disposal of materials is a local business, and the dynamics and opportunities differ in each market we serve. By combining local operational management with standardized business practices, we drive greater operating efficiencies across the company while maintaining day-to-day operational decisions at the local level, closest to the customer. Our customers, including small businesses, major corporations and municipalities, want a partner with the expertise and capabilities to effectively manage their multiple recycling and waste streams. They choose Republic Services because we are committed to exceeding their expectations and helping them achieve their sustainability goals. Our 42,000 team members understand that it's not just what we do that matters, but how we do it. Our company values guide our daily actions: Safe : We protect the livelihoods of our colleagues and communities. Committed to Serve : We go above and beyond to exceed our customers’ expectations. Environmentally Responsible: We take action to improve our environment. Driven : We deliver results in the right way. Human-Centered: We respect the dignity and unique potential of every person. We are proud of our high employee engagement score of 86. We have an inclusive and diverse culture where every voice counts. In addition, our team positively impacted 5.1 million people in 2024 through the Republic Services Charitable Foundation and local community grants. These projects are designed to meet the specific needs of the communities we serve, with a focus on building sustainable neighborhoods. STRATEGY Republic Services’ strategy is designed to generate profitable growth. Through acquisitions and industry advancements, we safely and sustainably manage our customers’ multiple waste streams through a North American footprint of vertically integrated assets. We focus on three areas of growth to meet the increasing needs of our customers: recycling and waste, environmental solutions and sustainability innovation. With our integrated approach, strengthening our position in one area advances other areas of our business. For example, as we grow volume in recycling and waste, we collect additional material to bolster our circularity capabilities. And as we expand environmental solutions, we drive additional opportunities to provide these services to our existing recycling and waste customers. Recycling and Waste We continue to expand our recycling and waste business footprint throughout North America through organic growth and targeted acquisitions. The 13 million customers we serve and our more than 5 million pick-ups per day provide us with a distinct advantage. We aggregate materials at scale, unlocking new opportunities for advanced recycling. In addition, we are cross-selling new products and services to better meet our customers’ specific needs. Environmental Solutions Our comprehensive environmental solutions capabilities help customers safely manage their most technical waste streams. We are expanding both our capabilities and our geographic footprint. We see strong growth opportunities for our offerings, including PFAS remediation, an increasing customer need. Sustainability Innovation Republic’s recent innovations to advance circularity and decarbonization demonstrate our unique ability to leverage sustainability as a platform for growth. The Republic Services Polymer Center is the nation’s first integrated plastics recycling facility. These innovative sites process rigid plastics from our recycling centers, producing recycled materials that promote true bottle-to-bottle circularity. We also formed Blue Polymers, a joint venture with Ravago, to develop facilities that will further process plastic material from our Polymer Centers to help meet the growing demand for sustainable packaging. We are building a network of Polymer Centers and Blue Polymer facilities across North America. Our customers are increasingly looking for decarbonization solutions, and we are leveraging our network of landfills to meet that need. Republic is committed to harnessing landfill gas, a natural byproduct of decomposing waste, and converting it to energy. Republic has partnered with renewable gas developers to construct Renewable Natural Gas (RNG) plants at our landfills, expanding beyond the 77 projects we currently have to make progress towards our goal to beneficially reuse 50% more biogas by 2030 (2017 baseline year). title: Oncology Data Specialist - Abstractor
jd_text: Here at Savista, we enable our clients to navigate the biggest challenges in healthcare: quality clinical care with positive patient experiences and optimal financial results. We partner with healthcare organizations to problem solve and deliver revenue cycle improvement services that enable their success, support their patients, and nurture their communities, all while living our values of Commitment, Authenticity, Respect and Excellence (CARE). Company Overview: Savista partners with healthcare providers to navigate their biggest challenges in healthcare and improve their financial strength by implementing integrated revenue cycle and registry solutions that help control cost, improve margins and cash flow, increase regulatory compliance and optimize operational efficiency . Savista employs over 4000 colleagues and serves more than 500 client sites nationwide . Job Summary: Oncology Data Specialist – Abstractor s are responsible to complete clinical data abstraction for all reportable & non-reportable primary sites of cancer according to the reporting and timeliness guidelines established by the CoC, SEER , State Registries and other Standard Setters as required . Position Expectations: Maintains Active ODS-C certification Meets productivity standards and quality benchmarks while assuring the confidentiality, accuracy and timeliness of all cancer-related health information encountered. Up-to-date on all current state and national reporting guidelines. Complies with all Savista/client HIPAA and other privacy requirements and regulations. Maintains compliance with client’s abstracting policies and procedures. Participates in training, CEU activities and continuous learning initiatives. Essential Duties & Responsibilities: Reviews EMR to identify cancer cases and abstract details including patient demographics, tumor location/size, diagnosis, treatment (surgery, chemo, radiation), and outcomes. Abstracts data into specialized medical software with supporting narrative information for patient demographics, diagnostic procedures, history and extent of disease, treatments, outcomes, follow-up data, physicians, and related information from various medical records. Tracks patients throughout their lifetime to document patient’s health, treatment and progression of disease. Provide cancer incidence, treatment and outcome information to appropriate databases. Ensure that data is accurate and complete. Participate in QA reviews and incorporate feedback to support skill development. Correct errors as needed. Consistent accuracy rate of 95% or higher. Manages databases, ensures data quality, and runs reports for internal and external use. Participates in special projects and studies, as assigned. Escalates clinical or technical questions appropriately. Participate in training less experienced peers and participate in QA activities and peer reviews. Monitors productivity as needed. Data Submissions: May coordinate required submissions from the State Registry and CoC. Minimum Qualifications and Skills: ​ Active ODS-C (Oncology Data Specialist – Certified) credential. Knowledge of latest guidelines from standard setters (CoC, SEER, and NAACCR), and the ability to apply them accurately. Must be able to meet deadlines and work with time constraints. Ability to multi-task and be flexible to adjust assignments as priorities change. Effective communication skills with supervisors and peers and appropriate communication with clients. Ability to organize and complete work in a timely manner with minimal supervision. Self-starter with the ability to work effectively within the role, independently and with other team members. Strong attention to detail and willingness to grow technical competencies. Preference will be given to those candidates who meet the criteria above, and who also have the following: Minimum of 2 years of current abstracting experience in a cancer registry. Experience in CoC-accredited or comprehensive cancer programs. Other Requirements: High-speed internet access and experience with remote access, set-up, and troubleshooting technical issues. Secure home office HIPAA compliant. This position is remote but may be required to be onsite as needed. Physical Requirements: Prolonged periods sitting at a desk and working on a computer. Must be able to lift up to 15 pounds at times. Note : Savista is required by state specific laws to include the salary range for this role when hiring a resident in applicable locations. The hourly range for this role is from $29 - $35 . However, specific compensation for the role will vary within the above range based on many factors including but not limited to geographic location, candidate experience, applicable certifications, and skills . skills. jd_text: Our associates celebrate lives. We celebrate our associates.
